🎯 Found it:

`e: android/build.gradle.kts:19:9: Unresolved reference: coreLibraryDesugaringEnabled`

My Kotlin DSL was wrong. In Kotlin DSL for AGP, it's:
```kotlin
compileOptions {
    isCoreLibraryDesugaringEnabled = true
}
```
(AGP 8 Kotlin DSL uses `isCoreLibraryDesugaringEnabled` — Boolean property with `is` prefix.)

The prototype job failure: "exit code 1" at test step, 13s — hmm, why? Maybe the configuration phase failure of :android project affects the WHOLE gradle build (both jobs run `gradlew` which configures ALL projects including :android!). Yes! Configuration happens for all projects — the unresolved reference in :android's build.gradle.kts fails configuration globally → prototype job also failed. That explains it.

Fix: `isCoreLibraryDesugaringEnabled = true`.

Also the local phantom shell pollution mystery is SOLVED: the "BUILD FAILED in 25s" text was coming from CI — wait no... The phantom output appeared in MY LOCAL bash. Hmm — but now I realize: the annotation file includes "BUILD FAILED in 25s" — identical string to my phantom local outputs! Coincidence? My local phantom said "BUILD FAILED in 25s" at the same time CI was failing with "BUILD FAILED in 25s"... There's no mechanism for CI output to appear locally.

Actually — WAIT. Now I get it! My local bash tool output... The polling commands I ran DID work; their output was likely correct at the time but the tool returned stale... no. Let me look again at the sequence: after I killed java 3136, MARKER worked, POLL worked, then a 700s poll returned "BUILD FAILED in 25s" instantly. That CI run #9 (295ae5a→...). Hmm — run 34473730614 finished 11:56; run f389130 (34475693543) started 12:15. The phantom "BUILD FAILED in 25s" first appeared around... whatever. The mechanism: my LOCAL gradle single-use daemon from the last successful local test — `--no-daemon` with `gradle.properties` org.gradle.jvmargs → forked single-use daemon... those exit after build.

You know what — here's a plausible mechanism: opencode's bash tool maintains a persistent shell; a previous long command was killed by timeout leaving the shell busy; subsequent commands queue... The returned "BUILD FAILED in 25s" is the tail of a QUEUED command's output — the killed 700s poll? No gradle there.

Honestly, the exact mechanism doesn't matter. The practical takeaway: long-running bash commands may garble; use short commands, and verify CI via webfetch. Moving on.

Fix build.gradle.kts: `isCoreLibraryDesugaringEnabled = true`, commit, push, verify via webfetch (bash only for git push — short command).

🎯 علت پیدا شد: در Kotlin DSL باید `isCoreLibraryDesugaringEnabled` باشد (نه `coreLibraryDesugaringEnabled`) — و چون خطای configuration در `:android` بود، **job پروتوتایپ هم** (که همه پروژه‌ها را configure می‌کند) شکست خورد. اصلاح:

Progress! Configuration passes now. The error is in my test file:

`CryptoOnDeviceTest.kt:84:28 Unresolved reference 'deviceId'`

Line 84 is in `buildBundle`: I used `deviceId = deviceId` — but the Device class parameter is named `deviceId: Int` — wait, constructor params: `private val context: Context, label: String, private val alias: String, name: String, deviceId: Int`. I didn't make deviceId a property (`private val`)! Only context and alias are `private val`. So `deviceId` and `label`/`name` are plain constructor params — accessible in init/constructor scope but NOT in member functions like buildBundle. `name` is used in `SignalProtocolAddress(name, deviceId)` in property initializer — that works (initializer scope). But buildBundle can't see deviceId.

Fix: make `deviceId` a property: `private val deviceId: Int` (and name stays param). In buildBundle, `deviceId = deviceId` — with property, fine. Careful: naming collision in named argument `deviceId = deviceId` — Kotlin resolves the left side as parameter name of PreKeyBundle, right side refers to this.deviceId — OK.

Wait, line 84:28 — `preKeyId = oneTimeEc?.id ?: PreKeyBundle.NULL_PRE_KEY_ID` no... line 84 is probably `deviceId = deviceId,` in the PreKeyBundle constructor call. Yes.

Also line ~94 `registrationId = store.localRegistrationId` etc fine.

Apply fix, push, wait, check via webfetch. Also to reduce roundtrips, double-check the rest of the test file for similar scope bugs: 
- `label` used only in dbFile init ✓
- `name` used in address init ✓ (initializer)
- `alias` is val ✓
- In test bodies: uses bob.storeOneTimeEcPreKey etc ✓.

One more possible issue later at runtime: `InstrumentationRegistry.getInstrumentation().targetContext` for a library androidTest — targetContext is the test app context ✓ has databases dir.

Also `context.getDatabasePath("proto_alice.db")` in assertion vs Device's dbFile `proto_alice.db` — in test 1 I named label "alice" → file proto_alice.db ✓ matches assertion.

Push.

# chatapp

پیام‌رسان امن بدون شماره تلفن/ایمیل — Android client + Cloudflare backend.

## وضعیت

| فاز | شرح | وضعیت |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 0 | تحقیق: SimpleX UI، libsignal، Cloudflare، ناسازگاری‌ها | ✅ انجام شد |
| Phase 0.5-A | Crypto prototype روی JVM با libsignal رسمی (۸/۸ تست) | ✅ سبز در CI |
| Phase 0.5-B | Android: SQLCipher store + AndroidKeyStore، تست instrumented روی emulator | ✅ سبز در CI |
| Phase 1+ | Cloudflare Workers / D1 / DO / R2 | ⏳ نیازمند تأیید |

## Crypto

- **libsignal رسمی** — `org.signal:libsignal-android:0.102.1` از مخزن رسمی
  [build-artifacts.signal.org](https://build-artifacts.signal.org/libraries/maven/)
  (Maven Central برای نسخه‌های جدید libsignal به‌روز نیست)
- **Java 21 / Kotlin ≥ 2.2** لازم است (bytecode و metadata کتابخانه)
- Prootکل فعلی libsignal شامل PQXDH است — one-time Kyber-1024 prekey اجباری در PreKeyBundle
- `coreLibraryDesugaring` برای libsignal-android فعال است (الزام AAR metadata)
- AAR metadata: libsignal-android 0.102.1 → minCompileSdk=34؛ sqlcipher-android ≥4.18 → minCompileSdk=37 (به همین دلیل 4.17.0 پین شد)

## ساختار

```
prototype/   — Phase 0.5-A: JVM prototype (Store با serialized bytes = شبیه‌ساز Room)
android/     — Phase 0.5-B: library module
  crypto/DatabaseKeyManager.kt       — passphrase تصادفی + wrap با AndroidKeyStore (AES-GCM, non-exportable)
  crypto/SqlCipherProtocolStore.kt   — پیاده‌سازی کامل SignalProtocolStore روی SQLCipher
  androidTest/                       — تست instrumented روی emulator (CI)
```

## چیزی که تست‌ها اثبات می‌کنند

- identity per-device، SignedPreKey + KyberPreKey + OneTimePreKey، برقراری session (PQXDH)
- encrypt/decrypt هر دو مسیر (PreKeySignalMessage → SignalMessage) و گذار درست TYPE ها
- replay protection (DuplicateMessageException) و TOFU identity trust (UntrustedIdentityException)
- مصرف one-time prekeyها بعد از decrypt
- **persistence کامل بعد از restart**: بستن و باز کردن دیتابیس + unwrap passphrase از Keystore
- فایل دیتابیس روی دیسک **SQLite plaintext نیست** (SQLCipher فعال)
- identical بودن behavior بین JVM prototype و Android instrumented tests

## Build

- JDK 21 (Temurin) — `./gradlew :prototype:test` و `./gradlew :android:connectedAndroidTest`
- تست‌ها در GitHub Actions اجرا می‌شوند (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- محلی برای اندروید نیاز به Android SDK است؛ compileSdk 35, minSdk 26

## License

AGPL-3.0 — این پروژه به libsignal (AGPLv3) متصل است؛ کل اپ باید AGPLv3 منتشر شود.

# ✅ Phase 0.5-B کامل شد — هر دو job سبز در GitHub Actions

## وضعیت نهایی
- **Repo:** https://github.com/rezaarbab/chatapp (branch `main`، کامیت `dbf5f1e`)
- **CI:** 🟢 `prototype-tests: success` + `android-instrumented: success` (روی emulator واقعی API 34)
- آخرین اجرای سبز: https://github.com/rezaarbab/chatapp/actions/runs/34477449946

## چه چیزی روی دستگاه Android اثبات شد (تست instrumented)

1. ✅ ناتیو libsignal-android 0.102.1 روی اندروید لود و کل جریان protocol کار می‌کند
2. ✅ `SignalProtocolStore` کامل روی **SQLCipher** پیاده شد (همه ۶ interface شامل SenderKeyStore)
3. ✅ Passphrase تصادفی 32بایتی با **AndroidKeyStore** (AES-GCM، non-exportable) wrap می‌شود — هرگز plaintext روی دیسک نیست
4. ✅ **restart واقعی**: بستن دیتابیس → unwrap دوباره از Keystore → باز کردن → session سالم و decrypt موفق
5. ✅ فایل دیتابیس روی دیسک **magic مربوط به SQLite plaintext ندارد** (رمزنگاری فعال است)

# Migrations

Last updated Jun 8, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/reference/migrations/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/)

Database migrations are a way of versioning your database. Each migration is stored as an `.sql` file in your `migrations` folder. The `migrations` folder is created in your project directory when you create your first migration. This enables you to store and track changes throughout database development.

## Features

Currently, the migrations system aims to be simple yet effective. With the current implementation, you can:

* [Create](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/d1/#d1-migrations-create) an empty migration file.
* [List](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/d1/#d1-migrations-list) unapplied migrations.
* [Apply](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/wrangler/commands/d1/#d1-migrations-apply) remaining migrations.

Every migration file in the `migrations` folder has a specified version number in the filename. Files are listed in sequential order. Every migration file is an SQL file where you can specify queries to be run.

Binding name vs Database name

When running a migration script, you can use either the binding name or the database name.

However, the binding name can change, whereas the database name cannot. Therefore, to avoid accidentally running migrations on the wrong binding, you may wish to use the database name for D1 migrations.

## Wrangler customizations

By default, migrations are created in the `migrations/` folder in your Worker project directory. Creating migrations will keep a record of applied migrations in the `d1_migrations` table found in your database.

This location and table name can be customized in your Wrangler file, inside the D1 binding.

```jsonc
{
	"d1_databases": [
		{
			"binding": "<BINDING_NAME>", // i.e. if you set this to "DB", it will be available in your Worker at `env.DB`
			"database_name": "<DATABASE_NAME>",
			"database_id": "<UUID>",
			"preview_database_id": "<UUID>",
			"migrations_table": "<d1_migrations>", // Customize this value to change your applied migrations table name
			"migrations_dir": "<FOLDER_NAME>", // Specify your custom migration directory
			"migrations_pattern": "<GLOB>" // Optional: discover migrations using a glob pattern (see below)
		}
	]
}
```

```toml
[[d1_databases]]
binding = "<BINDING_NAME>"
database_name = "<DATABASE_NAME>"
database_id = "<UUID>"
preview_database_id = "<UUID>"
migrations_table = "<d1_migrations>"
migrations_dir = "<FOLDER_NAME>"
migrations_pattern = "<GLOB>"
```

## Nested migration layouts

By default, `wrangler d1 migrations apply` looks for top-level `.sql` files inside `migrations_dir`. If you use an ORM such as [Drizzle ↗](https://orm.drizzle.team/) that writes each migration as its own subdirectory (for example, `migrations/0001_init/migration.sql`), set `migrations_pattern` to the glob that matches your layout:

```jsonc
{
	"d1_databases": [
		{
			"binding": "DB",
			"database_name": "my-database",
			"database_id": "<UUID>",
			"migrations_dir": "migrations",
			"migrations_pattern": "migrations/*/migration.sql"
		}
	]
}
```

```toml
[[d1_databases]]
binding = "DB"
database_name = "my-database"
database_id = "<UUID>"
migrations_dir = "migrations"
migrations_pattern = "migrations/*/migration.sql"
```

Rules for `migrations_pattern`:

* When set, `migrations_dir` must also be set.
* The pattern must start with whatever `migrations_dir` is set to.
* Each migration's name is recorded in the migrations table as the path relative to `migrations_dir` (for example, `0001_init/migration.sql`). This keeps the table portable across machines.

The pattern is a standard glob — `*` matches one path segment, `**` matches any number of segments. `migrations/**/*.sql` will pick up arbitrarily deep `.sql` files.

`wrangler d1 migrations create` only writes top-level files inside `migrations_dir`, so if your `migrations_pattern` only matches nested files (as with the Drizzle layout), generate new migrations using your ORM's command (for example, `drizzle-kit generate`) instead.

## Foreign key constraints

When applying a migration, you may need to temporarily disable [foreign key constraints](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/sql-api/foreign-keys/). To do so, call `PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = true` before making changes that would violate foreign keys.

Refer to the [foreign key documentation](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/sql-api/foreign-keys/) to learn more about how to work with foreign keys and D1.

```sql
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  key_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  public_key BLOB NOT NULL,              -- KEMPublicKey serialize
  signature  BLOB NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at    INTEGER,
  UNIQUE (device_id, key_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_kyber_prekeys_pop ON kyber_prekeys(device_id, used_at, key_id);
```

Note: NO private keys of any prekey on the server ✓ principle 2.

```sql
-- 0004_messages.sql
CREATE TABLE message_queue (
  delivery_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,     -- UUIDv4 (per recipient-device row)
  logical_msg_id   TEXT NOT NULL,        -- client-generated (idempotency)
  sender_dev_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  recipient_dev_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  seq              INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- per-recipient monotonic order
  ciphertext       BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(ciphertext) <= 1900000),
  state            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (state IN ('queued','delivered')),
  server_recv_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at       INTEGER NOT NULL,     -- server-set TTL
  UNIQUE (sender_dev_id, logical_msg_id) -- idempotent POST /messages
);
CREATE INDEX idx_mq_recipient ON message_queue(recipient_dev_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX idx_mq_expiry ON message_queue(expires_at);
```

Hmm — seq allocation: per recipient device within a fan-out batch. For POST /messages with N recipient devices: one batch: for each recipient: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1? Multiple messages concurrently to same recipient — D1 single-threaded per DB + batch atomic → sequential batches get increasing seq. But two concurrent POSTs could compute same MAX+1 if both SELECT before either INSERT — within batch the SELECT+INSERT are in one transaction; two batches serialize (single-threaded DB) → safe. Actually D1 batch = one transaction; concurrent batches serialize at the DB (backed by single DO). ✓

```sql
-- 0005_attachments.sql
CREATE TABLE attachments (
  attachment_id  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,       -- UUIDv4
  sender_dev_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  r2_key         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- random object key; no plaintext metadata
  encrypted_size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  state          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (state IN ('pending','ready')),
  server_recv_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at     INTEGER NOT NULL        -- server-set TTL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_attachments_expiry ON attachments(expires_at);

CREATE TABLE attachment_delivery (
  attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(attachment_id),
  device_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  delivered_at  INTEGER,
  acked_at      INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, device_id)
);

-- 0006_backups.sql
CREATE TABLE backups (
  backup_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  account_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
  r2_key         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  encrypted_size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  backup_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_at     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at     INTEGER NOT NULL        -- TTL: only latest kept (policy)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_backups_account ON backups(account_id, created_at);

-- 0007_auth.sql
CREATE TABLE auth_challenges (
  challenge_id  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,        -- UUIDv4
  nonce         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,    -- 256-bit random, hex
  purpose       TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('register','auth','add_device')),
  account_id    TEXT,                    -- NULL for register
  device_id     TEXT,                    -- NULL for register/add_device
  identity_pub  BLOB,                    -- required for register/add_device (new device key)
  issued_at     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at       INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX idx_challenges_expiry ON auth_challenges(expires_at);

CREATE TABLE auth_tokens (
  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,           -- SHA-256(token); raw token never stored
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  issued_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,           -- server-set, short-lived
  revoked_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX idx_tokens_device ON auth_tokens(device_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_tokens_expiry ON auth_tokens(expires_at);
```

Endpoints (final API proposal):

Public:
- POST /auth/challenge  {purpose, username?, identity_pub?} → {challenge_id, nonce, expires_at}
- POST /accounts        {username, identity_pub, registration_id, label?, challenge_id, signature} → {account_id, device_id, token}
- POST /auth/verify     {challenge_id, signature} → {token, device_id, expires_at}

Authenticated (Bearer token; device from token context):
- POST /devices          {identity_pub, registration_id, label?, challenge_id, signature} → {device_id, token?} (new device gets own token via its own challenge... design: the NEW device performs add_device challenge flow itself: POST /auth/challenge {purpose:add_device, username, identity_pub}; but who authorizes adding a device? An existing device must approve (signed authorization from an active device of the account). Design: challenge add_device + auth_code? For MVP: existing device signs the "add_device" authorization: body includes authorizer_device signature. Keep in Phase 2 detail; schema supports.)
- DELETE /devices/{device_id}
- PUT  /devices/me/prekey-bundle  {signed_prekey:{key_id,public_key,signature}, kyber_prekeys:[...], one_time_prekeys:[...]}
- GET  /devices/{device_id}/prekey-bundle → {registration_id, identity_key, signed_prekey, kyber_prekey, one_time_prekey?} (atomic pops)
- POST /messages  {logical_msg_id, recipients:[{device_id, ciphertext}]} → {delivery_ids}
- GET  /messages?limit=50 → [{delivery_id, seq, sender_dev_id, ciphertext, ...}]
- POST /messages/{delivery_id}/ack
- POST /attachments/initiate {encrypted_size} → {attachment_id, upload: POST /attachments/{id}/upload}
- POST /attachments/{id}/upload (raw ciphertext body ≤ limit)
- POST /attachments/{id}/complete
- GET  /attachments/{id} (stream; only devices in delivery list)
- POST /attachments/{id}/ack
- POST /backups {envelope} → upload; GET /backups/latest
- GET  /ws (WebSocket upgrade → RealtimeHub DO)

Rate limits table (soft binding + strict D1 counters where noted).

TTLs proposal: challenge 5 min; token 24h; message 7d; attachment 7d; backup keep-latest 30d? propose.

DO: RealtimeHub per device_id — hibernation, serializeAttachment {device_id}, no state in memory. Notify flow: after fan-out batch commit, Worker calls DO fetch (fire-and-forget via waitUntil? or ctx.waitUntil) → DO pushes {type:"new_message"} minimal envelope (no ciphertext via WS push? Server pushes only a signal; client then GETs /messages. This keeps WS payload tiny and avoids duplication logic.)

Capacity estimate (free tier): 100 users × 100 msgs/day avg = 10k deliveries → 10k writes/day + overhead ≈ 30k writes/day ≪ 100k/day ✓. Reads: each device polls/fetch + WS → few ×10k rows ≪ 5M/day ✓.

# Phase 1 — Backend Architecture & D1 Design (DESIGN ONLY — not implemented)

Status: design awaiting approval. No backend code has been written.
Scope: Cloudflare Workers + D1 + Durable Objects (WebSocket Hibernation) + R2.
Verified platform facts used here are listed in §9.

---

## 1. Component overview

```
Android client (libsignal 0.102.1, Room/SQLCipher local store)
        │  HTTPS (JSON, Bearer token) + WSS
        ▼
Cloudflare Worker  ── routing / auth / validation / rate limiting
   ├── D1 (SQL)              accounts, devices, prekeys, message_queue, attachments, auth
   ├── Durable Object        RealtimeHub — one instance per device, WebSocket Hibernation
   ├── R2                    encrypted attachment blobs + encrypted backups
   └── Cron Trigger (hourly) TTL cleanup (D1 rows + R2 objects)
```

Design principles enforced by architecture:

| # | Principle | Mechanism |
|---|-----------|-----------|
| 1 | Server never sees plaintext messages/files | Only opaque ciphertext BLOBs; keys travel inside E2EE payloads |
| 2 | Private keys never leave devices | D1 stores prekey **public** keys only |
| 3 | No custom crypto | libsignal does all crypto; Worker does zero cryptography |
| 4 | Session state never on server | Server stores only opaque ciphertext |
| 5 | Files encrypted before upload | R2 holds client-encrypted blobs only |
| 6 | Delivery state is temporary | message_queue rows deleted on ACK or TTL |
| 7 | Delete after valid ACK | ACK verifies ownership against token |
| 8 | TTL set by server | `expires_at` computed by Worker constants; client cannot set it |
| 9 | device identity from token | `auth_tokens` table; `Authorization: Bearer` → device_id |
| 10 | ACK verifies ownership + is idempotent | Row owner check; repeated ACK returns success |
| 11 | Sensitive ops idempotent | `UNIQUE(sender_dev_id, logical_msg_id)` on message enqueue |
| 12 | Inactive devices revoked | `revoked_at`; excluded from fan-out snapshot; WS closed on revoke |

---

## 2. D1 schema (final proposal)

Conventions: UUIDv4 strings for public IDs; timestamps = unix epoch **milliseconds**;
BLOBs store official libsignal serialized bytes.

### 2.1 accounts

```sql
CREATE TABLE accounts (
  account_id  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  username    TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- exact match, case-sensitive (anti-enumeration: single lookup path)
  created_at  INTEGER NOT NULL
);
```

### 2.2 devices

```sql
CREATE TABLE devices (
  device_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,            -- public identifier (UUIDv4)
  account_id       TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
  dev_no           INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (dev_no BETWEEN 1 AND 127),
  -- dev_no = SignalProtocolAddress.deviceId. Range 1..127 is a libsignal constraint.
  -- NEVER reused, even after revocation (matches Signal semantics; avoids session collisions).
  identity_pub_key BLOB NOT NULL,               -- device-level identity (verified fact: each device has its own keypair)
  registration_id  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (registration_id BETWEEN 1 AND 16380),
  label            TEXT,
  created_at       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_seen_at     INTEGER,
  revoked_at       INTEGER,                     -- NULL = active
  UNIQUE (account_id, dev_no)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_devices_account ON devices(account_id, revoked_at);
```

Allocation of `dev_no`: next free number via
`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(dev_no),0)+1 ...` inside the same D1 batch as the INSERT
(D1 is single-threaded per database → batch is atomic). When 127 device rows
exist, registration fails with a policy error (MVP: acceptable for ~100 users).

### 2.3 prekeys (public keys only — never private keys)

```sql
CREATE TABLE signed_prekeys (
  id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  key_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  public_key BLOB NOT NULL,
  signature  BLOB NOT NULL,      -- verified client-side by libsignal at session build (not by Worker)
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  UNIQUE (device_id, key_id)
);

CREATE TABLE one_time_prekeys (
  id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  key_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  public_key BLOB NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at    INTEGER,             -- set atomically when served in a bundle
  UNIQUE (device_id, key_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_otp_pop ON one_time_prekeys(device_id, used_at, key_id);

CREATE TABLE kyber_prekeys (
  id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  key_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  public_key BLOB NOT NULL,      -- KEM public key (PQXDH — mandatory in PreKeyBundle)
  signature  BLOB NOT NULL,
  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at    INTEGER,
  UNIQUE (device_id, key_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_kyber_pop ON kyber_prekeys(device_id, used_at, key_id);
```

Atomic one-time prekey pop (single statement; D1 `batch()` makes pop+fetch atomic):

```sql
UPDATE one_time_prekeys
   SET used_at = :now
 WHERE device_id = :device
   AND used_at IS NULL
   AND key_id = (SELECT key_id FROM one_time_prekeys
                  WHERE device_id = :device AND used_at IS NULL
                  ORDER BY key_id LIMIT 1)
RETURNING key_id, public_key;
-- identical pattern for kyber_prekeys
```

If one-time keys are exhausted, the bundle is served with signed + kyber
last-resort keys only. **Prototype-proven:** libsignal accepts a bundle with
`preKeyId = NULL_PRE_KEY_ID` and still establishes a session (Phase 0.5 test 6).

### 2.4 message queue

```sql
CREATE TABLE message_queue (
  delivery_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- per recipient-device row (fan-out)
  logical_msg_id   TEXT NOT NULL,             -- client-generated; idempotency key
  sender_dev_id    TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  recipient_dev_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  seq              INTEGER NOT NULL,          -- per-recipient monotonic order
  ciphertext       BLOB NOT NULL CHECK (length(ciphertext) <= 1900000),
  state            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'queued' CHECK (state IN ('queued','delivered')),
  server_recv_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at       INTEGER NOT NULL,          -- server-set TTL (client input ignored)
  UNIQUE (sender_dev_id, logical_msg_id)      -- idempotent enqueue
);
CREATE INDEX idx_mq_inbox ON message_queue(recipient_dev_id, seq);
CREATE INDEX idx_mq_expiry ON message_queue(expires_at);
```

`seq` allocation: inside the same atomic batch as the INSERTs,
`SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq),0)+1 FROM message_queue WHERE recipient_dev_id = ?`
per recipient. Safe because a D1 database is single-threaded and `batch()` is
one transaction → concurrent POSTs serialize.

Fan-out = snapshot semantics: recipients = active devices **at send time**
(`revoked_at IS NULL`). Devices registered later do not receive old messages.
Each recipient device gets an independent row → independent delivery + ACK.

### 2.5 attachments & backups

```sql
CREATE TABLE attachments (
  attachment_id  TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  sender_dev_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  r2_key         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- random key; stores NO plaintext filename/mime/keys
  encrypted_size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  state          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (state IN ('pending','ready')),
  server_recv_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at     INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_att_expiry ON attachments(expires_at);

CREATE TABLE attachment_delivery (
  attachment_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES attachments(attachment_id),
  device_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  delivered_at  INTEGER,
  acked_at      INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (attachment_id, device_id)
);

CREATE TABLE backups (
  backup_id      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  account_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
  r2_key         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  encrypted_size INTEGER NOT NULL,
  backup_version INTEGER NOT NULL,
  created_at     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at     INTEGER NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX idx_backups_account ON backups(account_id, created_at);
```

### 2.6 auth

```sql
CREATE TABLE auth_challenges (
  challenge_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  nonce        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,    -- 256-bit random
  purpose      TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (purpose IN ('register','auth','add_device')),
  account_id   TEXT,                    -- NULL for 'register'
  device_id    TEXT,                    -- NULL for 'register'/'add_device'
  identity_pub BLOB,                    -- required for register/add_device (new device identity)
  issued_at    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  used_at      INTEGER                  -- atomic single-use: UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL
);

CREATE TABLE auth_tokens (
  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,          -- SHA-256(token); raw token never stored server-side
  device_id  TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id),
  issued_at  INTEGER NOT NULL,
  expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL,          -- short-lived, server-set
  revoked_at INTEGER
);
CREATE INDEX idx_tokens_device ON auth_tokens(device_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_tokens_expiry ON auth_tokens(expires_at);
```

Signed data for challenges (canonical string, `\n`-joined):

- `register`:    `"register\n" + challenge_id + "\n" + nonce + "\n" + username`
- `auth`:        `"auth\n" + challenge_id + "\n" + nonce`
- `add_device`:  `"add_device\n" + challenge_id + "\n" + nonce + "\n" + username + "\n" + base64(identity_pub)`
  Signature produced by libsignal `ECPrivateKey.calculateSignature` (Curve25519 signature — verified
  in the Phase 0.5 prototype that this API exists and works).

Server-side verification note: Workers WebCrypto cannot verify Curve25519
signatures; adding that would be custom crypto. Therefore the Worker does NOT
verify prekey signatures — libsignal verifies them on the receiving client
during `SessionBuilder.process` (audited library path). Challenge signatures are
verified **by construction**: the private key holder is the only one who can
produce a key that later matches during E2EE identity binding; plus tokens are
only issued after signature checks that *are* possible server-side — see §4
open question Q3.

---

## 3. API surface (final proposal)

All bodies JSON unless noted. `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; device identity
always derived from token (never from body).

| Method & path | Auth | Purpose / notes |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/auth/challenge` | none | issue nonce (purpose: register / auth / add_device) |
| POST `/accounts` | none | create account + first device (dev_no=1) → returns token |
| POST `/auth/verify` | none | exchange signed challenge → token |
| POST `/devices` | token | add device to own account (requires `add_device` challenge signed by new device identity + approval signature from an active device) |
| DELETE `/devices/{device_id}` | token | revoke; closes its WS; excludes from future fan-out |
| PUT `/devices/me/prekey-bundle` | token | upload/replace signed + kyber (last-resort) + one-time keys |
| GET `/devices/{device_id}/prekey-bundle` | token | atomic pop of one-time EC + kyber keys |
| POST `/messages` | token | `{logical_msg_id, recipients:[{device_id, ciphertext}]}` → fan-out (store-first) |
| GET `/messages` | token | own inbox ordered by `seq`, `limit≤50` |
| POST `/messages/{delivery_id}/ack` | token | ownership check; idempotent (204 also when already gone) |
| POST `/attachments/initiate` | token | `{encrypted_size}` → `{attachment_id, expires_at}` |
| POST `/attachments/{id}/upload` | token | raw ciphertext body → R2 stream (≤ 50 MB MVP) |
| POST `/attachments/{id}/complete` | token | verify R2 object size → `state='ready'`; delivery rows created; file key travels inside E2EE message only |
| GET `/attachments/{id}` | token | stream from R2; allowed only to devices in delivery snapshot |
| POST `/attachments/{id}/ack` | token | per-device ack; delete when snapshot fully acked or TTL |
| POST `/backups` | token | encrypted backup blob → R2; keeps latest per account |
| GET `/backups/latest` | token | latest encrypted backup |
| GET `/ws` | token | WebSocket upgrade → RealtimeHub DO (idFromName = device_id) |
| GET `/users/{username}` | token | exact-match lookup only; constant-shape 404 |

Message delivery push = **signal only**: after fan-out commit, Worker (via
`ctx.waitUntil`) calls the recipient's RealtimeHub DO, which pushes
`{"t":"n"}` (a no-content notify). Client then GETs `/messages`. Keeps WS
payloads minimal and removes duplicate-delivery logic.

---

## 4. Authentication & token lifecycle

1. Client requests challenge (nonce = 256-bit random, TTL 5 min, single-use row).
2. Client signs canonical string with device identity private key (libsignal API).
3. Server atomically consumes challenge (`UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL`,
   check `meta.changes = 1`) → replay-proof.
4. Server issues token: `token = 256-bit random`; stores only `SHA-256(token)`;
   TTL 24 h; bound to device_id; revoked when device revoked.
5. Every request: constant-time hash lookup → device row must be active
   (`revoked_at IS NULL`) → updates `last_seen_at` (throttled).

Device revocation: DELETE /devices → `revoked_at=now`, revoke all tokens,
close WS (RealtimeHub enforces by checking device state on reconnect).

---

## 5. Real-time delivery (Durable Object)

- Class `RealtimeHub`, one instance per device (`idFromName(device_id)`).
- Uses **WebSocket Hibernation API** (verified docs): `ctx.acceptWebSocket()`,
  `webSocketMessage/webSocketClose` handlers, `serializeAttachment({device_id})`
  (well under the 16 KB limit).
- No in-memory state beyond connections → survive hibernation/deploy
  (deploy disconnects sockets — clients must auto-reconnect + GET /messages;
  store-first design makes this lossless).
- On notify: `stub.fetch()` from Worker after fan-out commit (fire-and-forget
  inside `ctx.waitUntil`).

## 6. TTL & cleanup (server-owned)

Proposed constants (require approval):

| Object | TTL / policy |
|---|---|
| auth challenge | 5 minutes |
| auth token | 24 hours |
| message_queue row | 7 days |
| attachment (R2 object + rows) | 7 days |
| backups | latest per account, older versions 30 days |
| one-time prekeys low-water mark | client uploads when < 25 remain (server hint in bundle response) |

Cleanup: **hourly Cron Trigger** (free tier: 5 crons/account, 15-min wall time —
verified) deletes expired rows; expired `ready` attachments delete R2 objects
first (free operation), then rows. Idempotent by construction.

## 7. Rate limiting (two layers)

Layer 1 — Workers **Rate Limiting binding** (verified: `simple{limit, period 10|60s}`,
per-PoP, eventually consistent) for soft per-key limits.
Layer 2 — strict D1 counters for security-critical limits (per-PoP leak must not
break anti-abuse): account creation, challenge issuance, auth failures.

| Operation | Soft limit (binding) | Strict counter |
|---|---|---|
| account creation | 3 / 10 min / IP-hash | 50 / day / global |
| challenge issue | 10 / min / device or IP | 500 / day / IP-hash |
| auth failure | 5 / 15 min / device | enforced in D1 (cooldown) |
| POST /messages | 120 / min / device | — |
| prekey bundle GET | 30 / min / device | — |
| prekey upload | 6 / min / device | — |
| attachment initiate | 30 / min / device | size ≤ 50 MB |
| WebSocket | 1 active connection per device | enforced by token |

## 8. Migration plan (wrangler D1 migrations — verified commands)

Layout: `backend/worker/migrations/*.sql`, applied via
`wrangler d1 migrations apply <db> --remote` (tracked in `d1_migrations` table).
Rules: migrations are append-only, never edited after apply; each migration is
one logical change; destructive changes get a dedicated migration + review.

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `0001_accounts.sql` | accounts |
| `0002_devices.sql` | devices + indexes |
| `0003_prekeys.sql` | signed/one-time/kyber prekeys + indexes |
| `0004_messages.sql` | message_queue + indexes |
| `0005_attachments_backups.sql` | attachments, attachment_delivery, backups |
| `0006_auth.sql` | auth_challenges, auth_tokens |

Planned repo layout:

```
backend/worker/
  wrangler.jsonc        # bindings: DB (D1), REALTIME (DO), FILES (R2), rate limits, cron
  src/index.ts          # zero-dependency router + auth middleware + error envelope
  src/auth.ts           # challenge/verify/token
  src/routes/*.ts       # accounts, devices, prekeys, messages, attachments, backups
  src/realtime.ts       # RealtimeHub DO (hibernation)
  src/cleanup.ts        # scheduled handler
  migrations/           # table above
  test/                 # vitest + @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers (local D1/DO/R2)
```

Deliberate choice: **no web framework** (Hono etc.) — ~20 endpoints; fewer
supply-chain dependencies for a security-critical component; typed helpers only.

## 9. Verified platform facts relied upon (from official docs, Sep 2026)

- Workers Free: 100k req/day, 10 ms CPU, 100 MB body, 5 cron triggers.
- D1 Free: 500 MB/db, 5 M row-reads/day, 100 k row-writes/day, 2 MB BLOB cap
  → ciphertext per message ≤ 1.9 MB; larger payloads must be attachments.
- D1: single-threaded per DB (backed by one DO), `batch()` = atomic transaction.
- Durable Objects on Free: SQLite-backed classes, alarms, WS message ≤ 32 MiB.
- WS Hibernation: `acceptWebSocket`, 16 KB serializeAttachment cap, auto
  ping/pong, deploy disconnects all sockets.
- Rate Limiting binding: `simple {limit, period: 10|60}`, per-PoP counters.
- R2 Free: 10 GB-month, deletes free, 5 GiB single-part upload.

## 10. Capacity estimate (100 users, free tier)

Assumption: 100 msg/device/day average → 10k delivery rows/day ≈ 30k D1 row
writes/day (messages + auth + acks) — ≈ 30 % of the 100k/day free write budget.
Reads negligible vs 5M/day. Storage: ciphertext ≪ 500 MB/db. Conclusion: MVP
fits comfortably on the free tier; paid tier needed only if attachment volume
exceeds R2 free tier.

## 11. Threat model mapping

| Threat | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Server compromise / admin | Only ciphertext, public prekeys, metadata (graph, sizes, timings) visible — documented residual risk |
| Network observer / MITM | TLS + E2EE; TOFU identity pinning client-side (libsignal) |
| Replay | Single-use challenges (atomic consume); libsignal DuplicateMessageException; unique `(sender_dev_id, logical_msg_id)` |
| Device impersonation | add_device requires new-device identity signature + active-device approval signature |
| Stolen token | 24 h TTL, server-side revocation, device-bound, only hash stored |
| Stored file access | R2 objects are client-encrypted; R2 metadata holds no filename/keys |
| Enumeration | exact-match lookup only, constant-shape errors, strict counters |

- **Q1 — TTLs:** accept the §6 table?
- **Q2 — Username:** case-sensitive exact match OK?
- **Q3 — Challenge signature verification:** Workers cannot verify Curve25519

  build, TOFU) and the server treats signatures as opaque. Alternative would be

  rule. Accept the indirect model?

- **Q5 — Push-as-signal WS design:** OK?

# 📐 گزارش طراحی Phase 1 — آماده و در repo ثبت شد

**سند کامل:** `docs/PHASE1_DESIGN.md` — https://github.com/rezaarbab/chatapp/blob/main/docs/PHASE1_DESIGN.md

هیچ implementation انجام نشد — فقط طراحی، migration plan و گزارش معماری.

## خلاصه تصمیم‌های کلیدی

### D1 Schema نهایی (اصلاح‌شده نسبت به draft شما)
- ➕ **`kyber_prekeys`** — الزام PQXDH (اثبات‌شده در prototype)
- ➕ **`dev_no INTEGER 1..127`** با `UNIQUE(account_id, dev_no)` — محدودیت واقعی `SignalProtocolAddress`؛ **هرگز reuse نمی‌شود**
- ➕ **`auth_tokens`** — فقط `SHA-256(token)` ذخیره می‌شود؛ device-bound؛ TTL 24h؛ revoke با revoke دستگاه
- ➕ `UNIQUE(sender_dev_id, logical_msg_id)` → idempotency واقعی POST /messages
- ➕ `seq` per-recipient برای ترتیب؛ `CHECK(length(ciphertext) ≤ 1.9MB)` (سقف واقعی BLOB در D1 = 2MB)
- ✅ هیچ private key prekey روی سرور نیست — فقط public
- ۶ migration مجزا: `0001_accounts` → `0006_auth` (append-only، wrangler d1 migrations)

### معماری
- **Worker بدون framework** (کاهش ریسک supply-chain؛ ~20 endpoint)
- **RealtimeHub DO** per-device با Hibernation؛ push فقط **سیگنال** است، محتوا با GET /messages
- **Cron ساعتی** برای TTL cleanup (D1 rows + R2 objects)
- Rate limiting دولایه: binding نرم + counters سخت D1 برای signup/challenge
- Pop اتمیک one-time prekey با `UPDATE...RETURNING` تک‌statement
- **fan-out = snapshot لحظه ارسال**؛ دستگاه‌های جدید پیام قدیمی نمی‌گیرند

## ⚠️ Q3 — مهم‌ترین نکته امنیتی برای تصمیم شما

Workers نمی‌تواند امضای Curve25519 را بدون crypto سفارشی verify کند (WebCrypto پشتیبانی نمی‌کند). دو گزینه:
- **پیشنهاد من:** سرور امضاها را opaque درنظر بگیرد؛ binding هویت به‌صورت TOFU سمت کلاینت در `SessionBuilder.process` انجام می‌شود (مسیر audit‌شده libsignal — در prototype اثبات شد)
- جایگزین: پیاده‌سازی verify سفارشی در Worker → **نقض قانون ممنوعیت crypto سفارشی**

The user rejected the TOFU-indirect model for Q3 and demanded a proper server-side-verifiable device authentication model, independent of libsignal identity:

Requirements from user:
1. Dedicated Authentication key per device
2. Don't conflate with libsignal Identity Key (unless official API/security model explicitly supports it)

11. Don't start Phase 1 implementation until this design + official API findings + threat analysis are reported

So now my task: **Device Authentication Key design**.

Key research needed:
1. **WebCrypto in Cloudflare Workers — Ed25519 support status.** Historically: Workers supported Ed25519 in beta ("Ed25519 in beta" via custom operation?) Actually Cloudflare Workers runtime (workerd) supports: ECDH (P-256, P-384, X25519?), HKDF, HMAC, RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5, RSA-PSS, ECDSA (P-256/P-384), and Ed25519 — I recall Cloudflare added Ed25519 support ( sign/verify, generateKey, exportKey) — as of 2023-2024, Ed25519 is supported in Workers (it's listed in their docs under "Supported algorithms" with notes; Ed25519 via "Ed25519" named curve is supported for sign/verify/derive? Let me verify via docs page: https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/security/... no — the right page: https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-crypto/ — lists supported algorithms. Ed25519 sign/verify — I believe supported (workerd implements it). Must verify by fetching docs.

2. **Android side**: WebCrypto isn't native on Android, but Java has `java.security`/`Signature` with Ed25519 — **Ed25519 in Android Keystore**: Android 13 (API 33+) added Ed25519 support to AndroidKeyStore (KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_ED25519? Actually Android 13 added "Keystore Ed25519" — yes: Android 13 (T) introduced support for Ed25519 in AndroidKeyStore (KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_ED25519). Before API 33, apps can use software Ed25519 (e.g., BouncyCastle/ed25519-java/Tink) — but that violates "no custom crypto"? Using a standard, audited library (Google Tink, or the platform java.security if provider supports) is acceptable — "standard and audited". Options:
   - API 33+ (Android 13): Ed25519 in AndroidKeyStore (hardware-backed where available) — private key non-exportable, sign-only.
   - API 26..32: Tink (Google, audited, standard) for Ed25519 software key, stored inside SQLCipher-encrypted DB, or key wrapped by Keystore AES-GCM key.
   - OR: use ECDSA P-256 — supported by AndroidKeyStore since API 23 (EC sign) AND WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 sign/verify in Workers. **This is the sweet spot**: one algorithm everywhere, hardware-backed keystore on all API 23+, official WebCrypto support in Workers. Ed25519 is nicer but Android Keystore support only 33+.

   User said "اگر Ed25519 در محیط هدف به‌صورت رسمی و مناسب پشتیبانی می‌شود، مدل challenge-response را بر اساس آن طراحی کن؛ در غیر این صورت یک راه‌حل استاندارد..." — Decision depends on: Workers WebCrypto Ed25519 official support + Android Keystore Ed25519 (API 33+) vs P-256 everywhere.

   Given minSdk=26 in our prototype, Ed25519-in-Keystore only covers API 33+; for 26-32 we'd need software keys (Tink). Mixed model = complexity. P-256 ECDSA: Keystore since API 23 (setDigests SHA-256, SIGNATURE ECDSA), WebCrypto ECDSA in Workers (P-256) — fully standard, audited (NIST curve, FIPS), hardware-backed everywhere. Tradeoff: ECDSA signatures are malleable & require careful nonce — but Keystore handles signing internally (private key non-exportable) and WebCrypto verify is standard. That's the pragmatic, environment-supported choice. I'll present Ed25519 as alternative where supported, recommend **ECDSA P-256 + SHA-256** as primary for uniform support. But the user explicitly prefers Ed25519 if "رسمی و مناسب" — need to check Workers docs; if Workers Ed25519 is officially supported (it is, I believe — need the docs page), the remaining issue is Android Keystore pre-33. Hmm — the "محیط هدف" (target environment) includes both Workers AND Android. Since Android Keystore Ed25519 = API 33+ only, and our minSdk 26, Ed25519 would require software private keys on 26–32 devices (Tink — standard/audited but private key in SQLCipher, protected by Keystore-wrapped DEK — same protection level as libsignal keys). That's a viable design too: auth key software Ed25519 via Tink everywhere (uniform), or hybrid.

   Let me think about what's BEST:
   - Uniformity matters for security analysis. 
   - Hardware-backed (Keystore ECDSA P-256, API 23+) means the auth private key NEVER exists in app memory/DB — strongest device-binding; compromised app can't exfiltrate auth key (only sign with it). This is a big security win and matches "no key material outside keystore" philosophy for the AUTH key.
   - Ed25519 via Tink: key material in SQLCipher (software) — comparable protection to libsignal identity key today.
   - Recommendation: **ECDSA P-256 with AndroidKeyStore** (SIGN only, non-exportable, SHA-256withECDSA), verified server-side via WebCrypto ECDSA P-256 + SHA-256. Ed25519 noted as future option at minSdk 33.

Client generates Keystore EC P-256 keypair locally (no server involvement), exports public key (SPKI format via KeyInfo/X509EncodedKeySpec — Java: getEncoded() returns X.509/SPKI for public). Workers WebCrypto importKey("spki", ...) — WebCrypto ECDSA import expects raw/"raw" for public? WebCrypto importKey supports 'spki' and 'raw' for EC public keys (raw = uncompressed point). Java Keystore public getEncoded() = SPKI DER → importKey('spki') ✓. Signature format: Java Signature "SHA256withECDSA" produces DER-encoded ASN.1 signature; WebCrypto ECDSA verify expects **raw r||s (64 bytes)** format! Mismatch! Options: client converts DER→raw (parsing DER to r/s is "format conversion", not crypto primitive — acceptable, small helper; but "هیچ signature format سفارشی" — converting DER ECDSA sig to P1363 raw is standard, defined in WebCrypto spec ("IEEE P1363" format). It's not custom crypto; it's canonical formatting per standards. Alternatively use "SHA256withPLAIN-ECDSA" (BouncyCastle-specific) — no. On Android 33+ there's "SHA256withECDSA_InTruncate"? no. Hmm — Android Keystore Signature output is DER-encoded ECDSA (per platform). WebCrypto verify needs raw P1363. A tiny DER→raw converter = parsing standard ASN.1. Is that "custom crypto"? It's byte reformatting of standard structures — I'd argue acceptable and it's a well-defined standard (RFC 5480/SEC1 + WebCrypto P1363). But user said "هیچ crypto primitive، signature format یا verify سفارشی پیاده‌سازی نکن" — a DER→P1363 converter might be considered "signature format سفارشی"? It's the opposite of custom — it's converting between two STANDARD formats. Risky to assume user accepts.

   Alternative avoiding conversion: use Ed25519 where Keystore doesn't produce DER issues (Ed25519 = fixed 64-byte signatures, WebCrypto Ed25519 verify = raw 64). If Workers Ed25519 is officially supported AND we accept software Ed25519 keys via a standard library on Android (Tink), signature formats align perfectly with zero conversion.

   OR — reconsider: maybe Workers supports Ed25519 — verify. That's coherent and uniform: Device Auth Key = Ed25519 (Tink, standard audited lib), stored in SQLCipher, usable on ALL API 26+. Signature = raw 64 bytes = WebCrypto Ed25519 verify (if Workers supports it officially).

Android 13 added Ed25519 to Keystore (KeyProperties.KEY_ALGORITHM_ED25519 — hmm, actually I recall Android 13 Keystore added "curved Ed25519"? Let me not guess — I can check developer.android.com docs for KeyProperties KEY_ALGORITHM_ED25519. # Web Crypto

Last updated Apr 23, 2026|Copy as Markdown|[View as Markdown](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/web-crypto/index.md)|[Agent setup](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agent-setup/)

## Background

The Web Crypto API provides a set of low-level functions for common cryptographic tasks. The Workers runtime implements the full surface of this API, but with some differences in the [supported algorithms](#supported-algorithms) compared to those implemented in most browsers.

Performing cryptographic operations using the Web Crypto API is significantly faster than performing them purely in JavaScript. If you want to perform CPU-intensive cryptographic operations, you should consider using the Web Crypto API.

The Web Crypto API is implemented through the `SubtleCrypto` interface, accessible via the global `crypto.subtle` binding. A simple example of calculating a digest (also known as a hash) is:

```js
const myText = new TextEncoder().encode('Hello world!');

const myDigest = await crypto.subtle.digest(
  {
    name: 'SHA-256',
  },
  myText // The data you want to hash as an ArrayBuffer
);

console.log(new Uint8Array(myDigest));
```

Some common uses include [signing requests](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/examples/signing-requests/).

Caution

The Web Crypto API differs significantly from the [Node.js Crypto API](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/crypto/). If you are working with code that relies on the Node.js Crypto API, you can use it by enabling the [nodejs\_compat compatibility flag](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/nodejs/).

---

## Constructors

* `crypto.DigestStream(algorithm)` DigestStream

  * A non-standard extension to the `crypto` API that supports generating a hash digest from streaming data. The `DigestStream` itself is a [WritableStream](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/streams/writablestream/) that does not retain the data written into it. Instead, it generates a hash digest automatically when the flow of data has ended.

### Parameters

* `algorithm`string | object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/digest#Syntax).

### Usage

```js
export default {
  async fetch(req) {
    // Fetch from origin
    const res = await fetch(req);

    // We need to read the body twice so we `tee` it (get two instances)
    const [bodyOne, bodyTwo] = res.body.tee();
    // Make a new response so we can set the headers (responses from `fetch` are immutable)
    const newRes = new Response(bodyOne, res);
    // Create a SHA-256 digest stream and pipe the body into it
    const digestStream = new crypto.DigestStream("SHA-256");
    bodyTwo.pipeTo(digestStream);
    // Get the final result
    const digest = await digestStream.digest;
    // Turn it into a hex string
    const hexString = [...new Uint8Array(digest)]
      .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))
      .join('')
    // Set a header with the SHA-256 hash and return the response
    newRes.headers.set("x-content-digest", `SHA-256=${hexString}`);
    return newRes;
  }
}
```

```ts
export default {
  async fetch(req): Promise<Response> {

    const [bodyOne, bodyTwo] = res.body.tee();
    // Make a new response so we can set the headers (responses from `fetch` are immutable)
    const newRes = new Response(bodyOne, res);
    // Create a SHA-256 digest stream and pipe the body into it
    const digestStream = new crypto.DigestStream("SHA-256");
    bodyTwo.pipeTo(digestStream);

    const hexString = [...new Uint8Array(digest)]
      .map(b => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0'))
      .join('')
    // Set a header with the SHA-256 hash and return the response
    newRes.headers.set("x-content-digest", `SHA-256=${hexString}`);
    return newRes;
  }
} satisfies ExportedHandler;
```

## Methods

* `crypto.randomUUID()` : string

  * Generates a new random (version 4) UUID as defined in [RFC 4122 ↗](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4122.txt).
* `crypto.getRandomValues(bufferArrayBufferView)` : ArrayBufferView

  * Fills the passed `ArrayBufferView` with cryptographically sound random values and returns the `buffer`.

### Parameters

* `buffer`ArrayBufferView

  * Must be an Int8Array | Uint8Array | Uint8ClampedArray | Int16Array | Uint16Array | Int32Array | Uint32Array | BigInt64Array | BigUint64Array.

## SubtleCrypto Methods

These methods are all accessed via [crypto.subtle ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto#Methods), which is also documented in detail on MDN.

### encrypt

* `encrypt(algorithm, key, data)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with the encrypted data corresponding to the clear text, algorithm, and key given as parameters.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/encrypt#Syntax).
* `key`CryptoKey
* `data`BufferSource

### decrypt

* `decrypt(algorithm, key, data)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with the clear data corresponding to the ciphertext, algorithm, and key given as parameters.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/decrypt#Syntax).
* `key`CryptoKey
* `data`BufferSource

### sign

* `sign(algorithm, key, data)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with the signature corresponding to the text, algorithm, and key given as parameters.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`string | object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/sign#Syntax).
* `key`CryptoKey
* `data`ArrayBuffer

### verify

* `verify(algorithm, key, signature, data)` : Promise<boolean>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with a Boolean value indicating if the signature given as a parameter matches the text, algorithm, and key that are also given as parameters.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`string | object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/verify#Syntax).
* `key`CryptoKey
* `signature`ArrayBuffer
* `data`ArrayBuffer

### digest

* `digest(algorithm, data)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with a digest generated from the algorithm and text given as parameters.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`string | object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/digest#Syntax).
* `data`ArrayBuffer

### generateKey

* `generateKey(algorithm, extractable, keyUsages)` : Promise<CryptoKey> | Promise<CryptoKeyPair>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with a newly-generated `CryptoKey`, for symmetrical algorithms, or a `CryptoKeyPair`, containing two newly generated keys, for asymmetrical algorithms. For example, to generate a new AES-GCM key:  
```js  
let keyPair = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(  
  {  
    name: 'AES-GCM',  
    length: 256,  
  },  
  true,  
  ['encrypt', 'decrypt']  
);  
```

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/generateKey#Syntax).
* `extractable`bool
* `keyUsages`Array

  * An Array of strings indicating the [possible usages of the new key ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/generateKey#Syntax).

### deriveKey

* `deriveKey(algorithm, baseKey, derivedKeyAlgorithm, extractable, keyUsages)` : Promise<CryptoKey>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with a newly generated `CryptoKey` derived from the base key and specific algorithm given as parameters.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/deriveKey#Syntax).
* `baseKeyCryptoKey`
* `derivedKeyAlgorithmobject`  
  * Defines the algorithm the derived key will be used for in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/deriveKey#Syntax).
* `extractablebool`
* `keyUsagesArray`  
  * An Array of strings indicating the [possible usages of the new key ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/deriveKey#Syntax)

### deriveBits

* `deriveBits(algorithm, baseKey, length)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

  * Returns a Promise that fulfills with a newly generated buffer of pseudo-random bits derived from the base key and specific algorithm given as parameters. It returns a Promise which will be fulfilled with an `ArrayBuffer` containing the derived bits. This method is very similar to `deriveKey()`, except that `deriveKey()` returns a `CryptoKey` object rather than an `ArrayBuffer`. Essentially, `deriveKey()` is composed of `deriveBits()` followed by `importKey()`.

#### Parameters

* `algorithm`object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/deriveBits#Syntax).
* `baseKey`CryptoKey
* `length`int

  * Length of the bit string to derive.

### importKey

* `importKey(format, keyData, algorithm, extractable, keyUsages)` : Promise<CryptoKey>

  * Transform a key from some external, portable format into a `CryptoKey` for use with the Web Crypto API.

#### Parameters

* `format`string

  * Describes [the format of the key to be imported ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/importKey#Syntax).
* `keyData`ArrayBuffer
* `algorithm`object

  * Describes the algorithm to be used, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/importKey#Syntax).
* `extractable`bool
* `keyUsages`Array

* `exportKey(formatstring, keyCryptoKey)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

#### Parameters

* `wrapKey(format, key, wrappingKey, wrapAlgo)` : Promise<ArrayBuffer>

#### Parameters

  * Describes the [format in which the key will be exported ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/wrapKey#Syntax) before being encrypted.
* `key`CryptoKey
* `wrappingKey`CryptoKey

  * Describes the algorithm to be used to encrypt the exported key, including any required parameters, in [an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/wrapKey#Syntax).

### unwrapKey

* `unwrapKey(format, key, unwrappingKey, unwrapAlgo,  
 unwrappedKeyAlgo, extractable, keyUsages)` : Promise<CryptoKey>

  * Transform a key that was wrapped by `wrapKey()` back into a `CryptoKey`.

#### Parameters

* `key`CryptoKey
* `unwrappingKey`CryptoKey

  * Describes the algorithm that was used to encrypt the wrapped key, [in an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/unwrapKey#Syntax).
* `unwrappedKeyAlgo`object

  * Describes the key to be unwrapped, [in an algorithm-specific format ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/unwrapKey#Syntax).
* `extractable`bool
* `keyUsages`Array

  * An Array of strings indicating the [possible usages of the new key ↗](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/unwrapKey#Syntax)

parts.text:
The AOSP KeyProperties.java (main branch) shows key algorithms: RSA, EC, XDH, AES, 3DES, HMAC variants — **NO Ed25519 constant** in the Keystore KeyProperties (main branch). So Ed25519 in AndroidKeyStore is NOT part of the platform KeyProperties API (it's not there). My recollection about Android 13 Keystore Ed25519 was wrong — good thing I checked. (Android 13 added Keystore support for... actually it added "software Curved 数字"? No — the constants list is authoritative: no ED25519.)

So Ed25519 **hardware/Keystore path is NOT available** on Android via AndroidKeyStore. Ed25519 on Android = software library only (e.g., Tink — standard/audited Google library) with private key in SQLCipher-protected storage.

Options for the Device Authentication Key:

**Option A — ECDSA P-256 (EC) via AndroidKeyStore (official, API 23+):**
- Private key non-exportable, hardware-backed where available (StrongBox optional on API 28+)
- Officially in KeyProperties: KEY_ALGORITHM_EC ✓ (confirmed in source above)
- Sign via Signature "SHA256withECDSA" → DER-encoded signature output
- Workers WebCrypto: ECDSA P-256 sign/verify ✓ officially; BUT WebCrypto ECDSA verify expects raw P1363 (r||s, 64 bytes for P-256), NOT DER. Java Keystore outputs DER. → needs DER→P1363 conversion (standard format conversion per WebCrypto spec + SEC1; it's byte re-formatting, not a crypto primitive). OR importKey the pub as SPKI and... no — verify format is fixed raw. Actually wait — WebCrypto ECDSA signature format: per spec, ECDSA signatures in WebCrypto are "raw" r||s. Java "SHA256withECDSA" produces ASN.1 DER SEQUENCE{r,s}. So conversion is required. Is DER→P1363 conversion "custom signature format"? It's a deterministic, standard, well-specified transformation (RFC 5480 + WebCrypto). Many production systems do this. But the user explicitly said "هیچ crypto primitive، signature format یا verify سفارشی پیاده‌سازی نکن" — a DER→raw converter could be viewed as implementing a signature format. It's ~40 lines of pure ASN.1 parsing — auditable but IS custom code in the crypto path.

**Option B — Ed25519 via Tink (software, all API 26+):**
- Tink = Google's standard, audited crypto library (satisfies "استاندارد و audit‌شده")
- Ed25519 signatures = fixed raw 64 bytes → matches WebCrypto Ed25519 verify EXACTLY (importKey raw 32-byte pub) — zero format conversion
- Private key software-only: stored in SQLCipher DB (wrapped by Keystore DEK) — same protection tier as libsignal keys
- Server verify: officially supported Ed25519 in Workers ✓ (confirmed above)
- Uniform behavior across all devices API 26+
- Tradeoff: auth private key extractable-by-root (unlike Keystore EC) — mitigated by SQLCipher + DEK wrapping; threat model accepts compromised-device risk anyway

**Option C — Hybrid: Keystore EC P-256 (33+...) no.** Complexity high.

User's directive: "اگر Ed25519 در محیط هدف به‌صورت رسمی و مناسب پشتیبانی می‌شود، مدل challenge-response را بر اساس آن طراحی کن" — "مناسب" is key: Ed25519 IS officially supported by Workers (verified), and on Android via Tink (standard audited) — but NOT in AndroidKeyStore. Is that "مناسب"? The Keystore-hardware advantage is lost for the auth key; but user asked earlier "بررسی کن که ... Android Keystore دقیقاً از چه چیزی محافظت می‌کند" — they want precise statements.

I'll present BOTH and recommend:
- **Recommended: Option B (Ed25519 via Tink)** — single algorithm end-to-end, exact WebCrypto-compatible wire format (no conversion code), audited standard library, works API 26+ uniformly. Auth private key protection = SQLCipher + Keystore-wrapped DEK (documented clearly as software-tier).
- **Option A (ECDSA P-256 in AndroidKeyStore)** — stronger key protection (non-exportable, hardware) but requires standard DER→P1363 signature format conversion (standard, deterministic, ~40 lines) and P-256/ECDSA path.

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider Option A conversion requirement. Java's Signature with Android Keystore EC keys: "SHA256withECDSA" → DER. There's no platform API for raw. So yes conversion needed.

Hmm, one more idea for Option A without conversion: use X25519?? No — that's key agreement not signatures.

What about Ed25519 in newer Android Keystore — actually Android 13 DID add "Keystore support for Ed25519"?? My check of AOSP main KeyProperties shows NO ED25519 constant — that's authoritative for the public Keystore API. (There's Keystore2/KeyMint support for Ed25519 in the backend (KM_ALGORITHM_ED25519 exists in KeyMint HAL!), but the Java KeyGenParameterSpec API doesn't expose it — some OEMs?? Not reliable/portable. So no.)

Decision recommendation: **Option B** with clear threat analysis + Option A as documented alternative. The user gets precise answers to all 9 questions.

Now also design details to answer user's exact list:

1. **libsignal Identity Key** — used ONLY for: E2EE session establishment (PQXDH/Double Ratchet identity), TOFU pinning of remote identities, signing prekeys. NOT used for server auth.
2. **Device Authentication Key** — used ONLY for: signing server challenges (register, auth, add_device) → obtaining tokens. Not used in E2EE.
3. **Initial binding**: at register/add_device, the challenge context includes auth_pub (+ identity_pub + username); client signs with the auth private key; Worker verifies with the auth_pub submitted in the SAME request → proves possession, binds auth_pub↔device row. Key substitution analysis:
   - Registration (new account): there's no prior trust anchor — first registration is the trust root (like TOFU). Protection: username uniqueness; TLS; rate limits. An attacker cannot replace an existing account's keys because account already exists (username taken).
   - add_device: requires TWO signatures: (a) new device's auth key over its own context, (b) an active device of the account (whose auth key is already registered) signs the same challenge context authorizing the addition. Server verifies both via WebCrypto → no attacker substitution possible without an already-registered device key.
   - Auth key rotation: new key must be signed/authorized by the CURRENT registered auth key (key-change ceremony) or by another active device of the account; otherwise server rejects auth_pub update. (devices.auth_pub_key never silently overwritten.)
4. **Public key storage**: `devices.auth_pub_key BLOB` (raw 32-byte Ed25519 public key) in D1.
5. **Private key storage (client)**: Option B: Tink keyset (Ed25519 private), stored in SQLCipher DB (private_key table) — or directly as raw seed encrypted... Tink keyset handle serialized in SQLCipher table `device_auth`. Option A: AndroidKeyStore, never stored/exportable.
6. **Key material inside SQLCipher**: libsignal identity pair, session records, prekey records (private), Tink auth keyset (Option B), token cache? (no — tokens in memory/prefs? tokens are bearer secrets: store in SQLCipher too or SharedPreferences; recommend SQLCipher table), attachment file keys (E2EE envelope, cached in DB), SQLCipher passphrase itself is NOT in SQLCipher (it's wrapped by Keystore).
7. **Android Keystore protects**: (a) AES-256-GCM key that wraps the SQLCipher passphrase/DEK (as implemented), (b) [Option A only] the auth private key itself. Not: libsignal keys, Tink keyset (in Option B).
8. **Lifecycle/rotation**:
   - Auth key: no automatic rotation; rotation via signed key-change ceremony (old key signs new key binding; server updates atomically); recovery path (Phase 7 backup) may include auth keyset.
   - libsignal keys: signed prekey rotated (e.g., ≤ 30 days? client policy — actually per client policy; propose 30d), one-time replenished (<25), kyber last-resort rotated similarly, identity never rotated (device identity).
   - Tokens: 30-min TTL, silent re-auth via auth-key challenge (separate refresh design as user said).
   - Keystore DEK: never rotated; DB re-key possible via SQLCipher export (out of scope).
9. **Device revocation**: revoked_at set → all auth_tokens for device revoked (rows deleted/marked); RealtimeHub closes WS; device excluded from fan-out; auth_pub row retained (with revoked_at) so dev_no never reused and old sessions distinguishable; re-registration creates NEW device with new dev_no + NEW auth key.

**Challenge design (final):**
- POST /auth/challenge {purpose, username?, device_id?, identity_pub?, auth_pub?} → {challenge_id, nonce (256-bit), expires_at} — challenge TTL **60s** (user's value)
- Single-use: `UPDATE auth_challenges SET used_at=? WHERE challenge_id=? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at>?` → meta.changes==1
- Context (canonical, `\n`-joined, UTF-8, version prefix):
  - `v1|register|challenge_id|nonce|username|b64(identity_pub)|b64(auth_pub)`
  - `v1|auth|challenge_id|nonce|account_id|device_id`
  - `v1|add_device|challenge_id|nonce|username|b64(identity_pub)|b64(auth_pub)|authorizer_device_id`
- Verify: WebCrypto `importKey('raw', auth_pub, {name:'Ed25519'}, false, ['verify'])` → `verify({name:'Ed25519'}, key, sig, ctxBytes)`. Ed25519 signature = 64 bytes raw ✓ Tink output ✓ (Tink Ed25519Sign outputs raw 64-byte per RFC 8032 ✓ same standard).
- Token: 32B random; store SHA-256(token) hash as PK (Worker has SHA-256 ✓); **timingSafeEqual** for comparisons (verified non-standard Worker extension exists); TTL 30 min (user's value).
- Re-auth: token TTL 30min; client re-runs auth challenge silently (auth key available without user interaction; local biometric gating is UX layer). Refresh design = separate per user's note (Phase 2 detail).

Schema changes:
- devices: + `auth_pub_key BLOB NOT NULL` (raw 32B), maybe `auth_key_alg TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Ed25519'`
- auth_challenges: + `purpose 'register'|'auth'|'add_device'` ✓ already; + fields for context (username, identity_pub, auth_pub) — store what's needed to verify at verify-time WITHOUT trusting request: challenge row carries username/identity_pub/auth_pub so verify step doesn't re-accept client-supplied values (prevents context-swap).
- devices.key material none.

## 4. Authentication & token lifecycle

**Superseded by §13 (Device Authentication Key). §13 is the approved direction;
this section remains only for the message/token flow.**

1. Client requests challenge (nonce = 256-bit random, TTL **60 s** (user-approved), single-use row).
2. Client signs canonical context string with the **Device Authentication Key** (Ed25519 — see §13).
3. Server atomically consumes challenge (`UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL`,
   check `meta.changes = 1`) → replay-proof.
4. Server **verifies the signature via official WebCrypto Ed25519** (`crypto.subtle.verify`,
   Secure Curves — verified supported in Workers, §14) against the `auth_pub_key`
   registered for that device.
5. Server issues token: `token = 256-bit random`; stores only `SHA-256(token)`;
   TTL **30 minutes** (user-approved); bound to device_id; revoked when device revoked.
   Comparisons use Workers `crypto.subtle.timingSafeEqual`.
6. Every request: hash lookup → device row must be active (`revoked_at IS NULL`)
   → updates `last_seen_at` (throttled).

Device revocation: DELETE /devices → `revoked_at=now`, revoke all tokens,
close WS (RealtimeHub enforces by checking device state on reconnect).
