Index: .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml	
@@ -1,100 +1,139 @@
 name: deploy-staging
 
 # Deploys the Worker + D1 to the STAGING environment and runs real-Cloudflare
 # smoke tests. Requires two GitHub Actions secrets (never committed):
-#   CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN  — API token with D1:Edit + Workers Scripts:Edit
-#   CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID — account identifier (not a secret, kept out of git anyway)
+#   CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN  â€” API token with D1:Edit + Workers Scripts:Edit
+#   CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID â€” account identifier (not a secret, kept out of git anyway)
 # Until both are configured, this job skips itself.
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main]
   workflow_dispatch:
 
 jobs:
   deploy-staging:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       enabled: ${{ steps.guard.outputs.enabled }}
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: "22"
       - id: guard
         env:
           CF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CF_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           if [ -n "$CF_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$CF_ACCOUNT" ]; then
             echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           else
-            echo "::warning::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID not configured — staging deploy skipped"
+            echo "::warning::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID not configured â€” staging deploy skipped"
             echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           fi
       - name: Install worker deps
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         run: npm install --legacy-peer-deps --no-fund --no-audit > npm-install.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 25 npm-install.log; exit 1; }
       - name: Create D1 staging database (idempotent)
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler d1 list --json > d1list.json || echo "[]" > d1list.json
           if ! grep -q '"name": "chatapp-staging"' d1list.json; then
             npx wrangler d1 create chatapp-staging
           fi
           npx wrangler d1 list --json > d1list.json
           node -e "const l=require('./d1list.json');const d=l.find(x=>x.name==='chatapp-staging');if(!d)process.exit(1);console.log(d.uuid)" > d1-id.txt
           echo "D1 database: $(cat d1-id.txt)"
       - name: Render staging config
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         run: |
           sed "s/__D1_DATABASE_ID__/$(cat d1-id.txt)/" wrangler.staging.template.jsonc > wrangler.staging.jsonc
           echo "config rendered (database id not committed to git)"
       - name: Apply migrations to real staging D1
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: npx wrangler d1 migrations apply chatapp-staging --remote --config wrangler.staging.jsonc
       - name: Verify migrations landed on real D1
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler d1 execute chatapp-staging --remote --config wrangler.staging.jsonc --json --command "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'" > tables.json
           node -e "
             const out = require('./tables.json');
             const tables = (out[0].results || []).map(r => r.name);
             const need = ['accounts','devices','signed_prekeys','one_time_prekeys','kyber_prekeys','message_queue','attachments','attachment_delivery','backups','auth_challenges','auth_tokens','rate_limits'];
             const missing = need.filter(t => !tables.includes(t));
             if (missing.length) { console.error('missing tables:', missing); process.exit(1); }
             console.log('all 12 tables present on real D1');
           "
       - name: Deploy Worker to staging
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         id: deploy
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler deploy --config wrangler.staging.jsonc | tee deploy.log
-          url=$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.workers\.dev' deploy.log | head -1)
+          sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' deploy.log > deploy-clean.log
+          url=$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.workers\.dev' deploy-clean.log | head -1)
+          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
+            sub=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" \
+              "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/workers/subdomain" \
+              | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{try{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log(j.result.subdomain||'')}catch{console.log('')}})")
+            if [ -n "$sub" ]; then url="https://chatapp-staging.$sub.workers.dev"; fi
+          fi
+          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
+            echo "::error::could not determine staging URL"
+            tail -n 20 deploy-clean.log
+            exit 1
+          fi
           echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "staging url: $url"
-      - name: Run real-Cloudflare smoke tests
+      - name: Run real-Cloudflare smoke tests (with wrangler tail capture)
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
+        timeout-minutes: 7
         env:
           STAGING_URL: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
           STAGING_TOKEN_TTL_MS: "20000"
-        run: node test/smoke-staging.mjs
+          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
+          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
+        run: |
+          npx wrangler tail chatapp-staging --format pretty > tail.log 2>&1 &
+          TAIL_PID=$!
+          sleep 8
+          node test/smoke-staging.mjs 2>&1 | tee smoke.log || true
+          kill $TAIL_PID 2>/dev/null || true
+          sleep 3
+          echo "captured tail: $(wc -l < tail.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0) lines"
+          if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
+            grep -E "\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|TimeoutError|AbortError|Error:" smoke.log | head -n 12 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
+            exit 1
+          fi
+      - name: Dump wrangler tail on failure
+        if: failure()
+        working-directory: backend/worker
+        run: |
+          if [ -s tail.log ]; then
+            grep -iE "Exception|error|throw|Unhandled|\"outcome\"" tail.log | grep -vE "GET /devices/me -> 401" | head -n 15 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::TAIL: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
+          else
+            echo "::error::tail.log empty or missing"
+          fi
+          if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
+            grep -E "\[HTTP\]|\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|TimeoutError|AbortError" smoke.log | head -n 12 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
+            exit 1
+          fi

HUGE progress:
- D1 staging created ✅

- Worker deployed ✅
- Smoke tests FAILED — at step 11, instantly (10:50:30 → 10:50:30, 0 seconds). Instant failure = likely a script error (STAGING_URL empty?) — the deploy step output URL parsing may have failed, so STAGING_URL was empty → script exits with "STAGING_URL is required" exit 1.

The deploy step did succeed — but my URL grep may not have matched, or the URL pattern differs. wrangler deploy output prints "https://chatapp-staging.<subdomain>.workers.dev" — my grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.workers\.dev' should match. Unless the URL contains the subdomain with different chars. Hmm, instant failure though — the smoke script starts with waitUntilReachable which retries for 30s, not instant. So the failure was BEFORE: `STAGING_URL is required` → steps.deploy.outputs.url was empty.

Wait — actually there's a subtle issue: the deploy step writes `echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"` — but I set `id: deploy` on the STEP named "Deploy Worker to staging"? Let me check: I put `id: deploy` on the deploy step ✓ and smoke step references `${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}` ✓. Hmm but the smoke step condition is `if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'` ✓ ran.

So url was empty → grep didn't match. Maybe wrangler deploy output format: "Uploaded chatapp-staging (x.x sec)" and "Deployed chatapp-staging triggers (x.xx sec)  https://chatapp-staging.xyz.workers.dev". The grep should match... unless wrangler printed it with ANSI colors breaking the regex? With tee, ANSI codes might wrap the URL. My regex `https://[a-z0-9-]+\.workers\.dev` — ANSI escape codes could be adjacent... The URL itself is lowercase. Or the deploy output went to deploy.log via tee ✓ and grep ran on deploy.log ✓.

Also the annotations for this run would tell me — the smoke step has no annotation diagnostics... I need to look at the smoke step output. Since it's a plain run step (no ::error:: emission in smoke-staging.mjs except console.error), annotations may not show. Let me check annotations for the check-run of this job — the deploy-staging check run id: need it. The check_suite 93703624697 — find the check run. Let me fetch annotations. Actually simplest: make the smoke step print diagnostics and retry. But I can't see logs without auth...

Options to diagnose without logs:
1. The check-run annotations for deploy-staging job — GH creates an annotation only if steps use ::error::. My smoke script prints console.error (no annotation).
2. Better: add `::error::` emission + a diagnostics dump in the workflow, and also write the deploy.log as an artifact? Upload artifact of deploy.log for debugging... but I can't download artifacts anonymously (403 earlier).

Better: fetch the actual deployed worker URL myself! The deploy SUCCEEDED — the worker is LIVE. The workers.dev URL format: https://chatapp-staging.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev. I don't know the subdomain. BUT I can query the Cloudflare API anonymously? No — needs auth.

Hmm — but the smoke failure is instant (0s), so STAGING_URL empty. Two fixes:
1. Make the smoke script print why it failed as ::error:: so annotations show it.
2. Make URL extraction robust: wrangler deploy with `--json`? No such flag for deploy. Use `npx wrangler deploy ... | tee deploy.log` then grep BOTH with and without ANSI stripping: strip ANSI with sed first: `sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' deploy.log > deploy-clean.log`. Also add fallback: if url empty → emit ::error:: with tail of deploy.log (safe: deploy log has no secrets; it may contain account subdomain — that's semi-public anyway once live).

Actually even better: `wrangler deploy` prints the URL; but there's also `wrangler deployments list`? Or `wrangler triggers`? Alternative robust: after deploy, GET `https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CF_ACCOUNT/workers/subdomain` with the token → returns subdomain JSON → construct URL deterministically. That's precise:
```
sub=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_TOKEN" "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CF_ACCOUNT/workers/subdomain" | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log(j.result.subdomain)})")
url="https://chatapp-staging.$sub.workers.dev"
```
That's reliable. Add echo of url (fine to print — workers.dev URL is public once deployed).

Also improve smoke step: on failure, print diagnostics to ::error:: (e.g., first response statuses).

parts.text:
The stepLog lines ([STEP] ...) are console.log — they go to the step log, not annotations. The annotations only carry ::error:: lines. I need the [STEP] output. Options: emit ::error:: for each stepLog too — but that pollutes. Better: on failure, re-print recent STEP lines. Simplest: in smoke script, track step logs in an array and on failure print all of them via console.error with ::error:: prefix... The workflow greps smoke.log for FAIL lines only. Let me change the workflow diagnostics to also grep "STEP" lines (they're in smoke.log). Actually simplest: modify workflow smoke step to print ALL of smoke.log as annotations on failure — smoke.log is small (~20 lines). Change the grep to include STEP lines.

Let me update the deploy-staging workflow's failure diagnostics: 
```
grep -E "PASS|FAIL|STEP" smoke.log | head -n 25 | while ... ::error::SMOKE: ...
```
That will show every step's status — exactly what I need. Push and rerun.
`[STEP]` خطوط فقط در step log هستند (نه annotation). diagnostics را تغییر می‌دهم تا همه STEP/PASS/FAIL خطوط را به‌صورت annotation نشان دهد:

input.newString:
- name: Run real-Cloudflare smoke tests
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        env:
          STAGING_URL: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
          STAGING_TOKEN_TTL_MS: "20000"
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          node test/smoke-staging.mjs 2>&1 | tee smoke.log || true
          if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
            grep -E "STEP|PASS|FAIL" smoke.log | head -n 30 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.320s' "$l")"; done
            exit 1
          fi

Why would `/auth/verify` return 500 on real Cloudflare but pass in miniflare? Look at handleVerify:

```ts
const device = await requireActiveDevice(ctx.db, consumed.row.device_id);
...
const ok = await verifyEd25519(device.auth_pub_key, signature, new TextEncoder().encode(context));
```

`device.auth_pub_key` comes from D1 as a **BLOB**. On real D1, reading a BLOB column via `.first()` returns... a **string**? On real D1, BLOB values may be returned as... hmm. Actually in real D1, BLOB values come back as ArrayBuffer? or Uint8Array? In miniflare they come back as Uint8Array. On real D1, I believe BLOBs are returned as `ArrayBuffer`. Then `verifyEd25519(device.auth_pub_key, ...)` — importKey with an ArrayBuffer cast as BufferSource would still work...

Wait, but the 500 means an exception was thrown. `crypto.subtle.importKey("raw", pubRaw, ...)` where pubRaw is a string → would throw? If D1 returns the BLOB as an ArrayBuffer, `verifyEd25519` receives it as the parameter typed Uint8Array, and `importKey("raw", pubRaw as BufferSource, ...)` — an ArrayBuffer is a valid BufferSource! So import wouldn't throw...

Hmm, unless D1 returns BLOB as a **string** (base64?) no... Actually real D1 returns BLOB as `ArrayBuffer`? Let me think about what throws:

In `verifyEd25519`:
```ts
const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey("raw", pubRaw as BufferSource, { name: "Ed25519" }, false, ["verify"]);
```
If pubRaw is ArrayBuffer — works. If it's a string — importKey throws TypeError → caught by errorResponse → 500 INTERNAL ✓ matches!

So on real D1, `device.auth_pub_key` is likely returned as **string**? Hmm, actually I recall: D1 returns BLOB columns as **ArrayBuffer** in some versions... In miniflare, Uint8Array. If ArrayBuffer, importKey works... but wait — actually there's another candidate: `consumeChallenge` on real D1... no, that worked in the register flow (register consumed its challenge fine!). Register also consumed a challenge ✓ (201 created). So consumeChallenge works on real D1.

Difference in verify: `requireActiveDevice` reads `auth_pub_key` BLOB → passes to verifyEd25519. In the register handler, verification used `b64ToBytes(consumed.row.auth_pub)` — a proper Uint8Array from base64 (the challenge row stores pubs as TEXT base64!). That's why register verification worked.

So the fix: in handleVerify, if `device.auth_pub_key` is an ArrayBuffer, wrap in Uint8Array; if string... Actually the robust fix: convert whatever comes back to Uint8Array:
```ts
const pubBytes = device.auth_pub_key instanceof Uint8Array ? device.auth_pub_key : new Uint8Array(device.auth_pub_key as ArrayBuffer);
```
Handle both ArrayBuffer and Uint8Array (and possibly string→ treat as base64? No — BLOB comes back as ArrayBuffer on real D1).

Actually let me also handle the general case: `new Uint8Array(arrayBufferOrArrayBufferView)` works for both ArrayBuffer and TypedArray. For a string it would produce garbage lengths (string has no length in bytes...). `new Uint8Array("...")` → throws? `new Uint8Array(str)` → treats as object without length → empty? Actually `new Uint8Array("abc")` → TypeError? It would try to convert to number → NaN → length 0? For safety, detect typeof.

The same issue will affect `markKyberPreKeyUsed`, prekey-bundle GET (public_key BLOB), messages GET (ciphertext BLOB), etc. So I should write a helper `asBytes(v: unknown): Uint8Array` in util.ts and use it everywhere BLOBs are read:
- verify: device.auth_pub_key
- devices.ts: no BLOB reads yet
- future prekey/message reads

No — regB is a register — independent... unless accounts_ip count: register #1 + register #2 = 2 ≤ 3 ✓. Hmm, but the previous smoke RUN (2 minutes earlier) also did registers from the same runner IP? Different runner IP each job. But real D1 persists rate_limits across runs! Previous smoke run (e98f6d3, 8 min earlier) used accounts_ip from ITS runner IP — different IP though. Runners vary; could collide by chance. count for accounts_ip persists in the real D1 table! With limit 3/10min and repeated runs — plausible collision. Actually more precisely: smoke run #2 (34292da) failed at the same place but that run's register #1 PASSED... so rate-limiting regB... Actually wait — maybe regB failed due to... accounts_ip limit: this smoke run did 2 registers; previous run 8 min before did 2 registers FROM ITS RUNNER IP. If both runs' runner IPs happened to hash the same (no—different IPs hash differently)... The D1 rate_limits key = sha256(ip). Different runner IP → different key → no collision. So regB's 409/429 shouldn't happen... 

Hmm, alternatively the smoke script's regB: `sigB = signB64(privB, ctxB)` where ctxB uses `b64(crypto.getRandomValues(...))` as identity — WRONG! I regenerate a random identity for the context but chB.body challenge stored a DIFFERENT random identity → INVALID_SIGNATURE → 401! Yes! Look at the smoke script:

```js
const ctxB = buildContext("register", { ..., identityPubB64: b64(crypto.getRandomValues(...)), ... });  // ← NEW random → mismatch!
```

That's a genuine smoke-script bug — the ctxB identity must be the same one submitted. I need issueRegisterChallenge-style helper that returns identityPubB64. So "second account registered" failure = my test bug, not server bug.

So two real fixes:
1. **Server: D1 BLOB read normalization** (`asBytes` helper) for auth_pub_key in handleVerify — the Miniflare↔Cloudflare divergence the user asked me to catch!

3. **Smoke script: token1Expires from reg.body.token_expires_at** (test bug).

The only structural difference is the BLOB read. If D1 returned Uint8Array like miniflare, no 500. So yes — real D1 returns BLOBs differently (ArrayBuffer or string), and `importKey` threw (if ArrayBuffer, importKey actually accepts ArrayBuffer... hmm).

Hmm, let me reconsider: if ArrayBuffer, `importKey("raw", ab, ...)` works. So the throw must be something else. What else could 500 in handleVerify?

- `issueToken` → INSERT auth_tokens... fine.
- `requireActiveDevice` → .first() ✓
- `verifyEd25519(device.auth_pub_key, ...)`: if auth_pub_key came back as **string**? D1 JS API returns BLOB as... Actually I now recall clearly: **real D1 returns BLOB columns as `ArrayBuffer`**, and miniflare returns `Uint8Array`. importKey accepts both. So no throw there.

What else could throw on real D1 but not miniflare in handleVerify? `consumeChallenge` — worked for register ✓ (register handler consumed too). 

Hmm wait — did register consume work? Register: consumeChallenge → verify → createAccountWithDevice → 201 ✓. So consume works.

So what's left: `requireActiveDevice(ctx.db, consumed.row.device_id)` — `.first()` with SELECT account_id, auth_pub_key, revoked_at — fine.

`verifyEd25519(device.auth_pub_key, ...)`: if auth_pub_key is ArrayBuffer — importKey("raw", ArrayBuffer) — valid BufferSource ✓. Unless... `new TextEncoder().encode(context)` fine.

Hmm — unless auth_pub_key came back as a **string**! If real D1 returns BLOB as base64-encoded STRING in the JSON path... Actually yes! I now remember: real D1 (the HTTP-backed implementation) returns BLOB values as **base64 strings**? No wait — D1 client returns ArrayBuffer for blobs. Hmm.

Honestly the cleanest explanation stands: BLOB round-trip shape differs (ArrayBuffer vs string vs Uint8Array) and something in the chain threw. Rather than guess the exact shape, `asBytes()` handling ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array | string(base64) covers all. And the smoke rerun will prove it.

Actually — wait, one more strong candidate: `markKyberPreKeyUsed`... no, not in verify.

Also possible: `buildContext("auth", { accountId: consumed.row.account_id, ... })` — consumed.row.account_id could be NULL if... the auth challenge stored account_id ✓ (set at challenge creation from device lookup). Fine.

Also `authenticate`... not used in verify (public).

Let me also double check `verifyEd25519(device.auth_pub_key, ...)`: if the BLOB comes back as ArrayBuffer, `pubRaw as BufferSource` is a lie but runtime accepts ArrayBuffer → works. If it comes back as a **string**, importKey throws → 500 ✓ MATCHES. I'm fairly confident real D1 returns BLOB as ArrayBuffer though...

Hmm, alternatively the 500 is from `requireActiveDevice`'s `.first()` with BLOB select... no, first() just returns it.

OK — implement asBytes handling all three shapes, apply in handleVerify, and also fix the smoke script bugs (#2, #3). Also apply asBytes proactively where future BLOB reads will occur (none yet in code paths beyond verify).

Also — the expired-token test: with token_expires_at from reg.body.token_expires_at ✓.

Let me write the fixes:

1. util.ts: add `asBytes(v: unknown): Uint8Array`:
```ts
export function asBytes(v: unknown): Uint8Array {
  if (v instanceof Uint8Array) return v;
  if (v instanceof ArrayBuffer) return new Uint8Array(v);
  if (typeof v === "string") return b64ToBytes(v);
  if (v && typeof (v as ArrayBufferView).buffer === "object") return new Uint8Array((v as ArrayBufferView).buffer);
  throw new Error("unsupported binary shape from D1");
}
```

2. router.ts handleVerify: `const ok = await verifyEd25519(asBytes(device.auth_pub_key), signature, ...)`; import asBytes.

3. smoke-staging.mjs: fix ctxB identity reuse; token1Expires from reg.body.token_expires_at; the cross-account register helper — make issueRegisterChallenge return identityPubB64 (already does) and use it in the inline ctxB.

Push, rerun deploy. Then report Phase 1.5.

The smoke test step is hanging. The most likely cause: `waitUntilReachable` — it loops 10 times × 3s = 30s max. Not that.

The expiry wait: `wait = max(0, token1Expires - Date.now()) + 1500`. token1Expires = reg.body.token_expires_at = now + 20000. That's ~21.5s max. Not the hang.

What can hang? `main().catch` — no. Actually — could the smoke script be waiting on an HTTP fetch that never resolves? The real Cloudflare edge on a hanging request? Or... the `sleep` in waitUntilReachable... no.

Hmm — actually the step has run >8 minutes. The `wait` computation: `token1Expires - Date.now()`. `reg.body.token_expires_at` — is it a number? Yes, JSON number. But wait — could `token1Expires` be undefined because reg.body was parsed but token_expires_at missing? Then `Number(undefined) - Date.now()` = NaN → `Math.max(0, NaN) + 1500` = NaN → `sleep(NaN)` → setTimeout(NaN) = fires immediately. Not a hang.

What about stepLog on me1... no.

The real suspect: **the first smoke run's `wait` was ~80s** (challenge-expires bug) — that finished. This run: expiry wait ~21s. So >8min is something else: maybe `SELF`-like connectivity... or the worker URL now returns something that hangs? Possibly the worker itself is hanging on a request — e.g., D1 query hanging on real Cloudflare? Or... the smoke script `waitUntilReachable` uses GET /devices/me — if the worker returns 500 (crash loop) it keeps retrying 10 times then exits. Not a hang.

Hmm — could the deploy have replaced the worker while... Actually wait: `wrangler deploy` completed. The smoke test then ran. A fetch from the runner to workers.dev hanging for minutes can happen with cold start issues? Rare.

Let me just wait a bit more — the job-level timeout isn't set on this step, so it could hang indefinitely. If it hangs, I should add a timeout to the step (e.g., timeout-minutes: 5) and to fetch calls (AbortSignal.timeout).

Given the wait, most likely the smoke script IS stuck in waitUntilReachable — wait, that exits after 10 attempts (30s). Hmm, but only if fetch() resolves. If fetch() itself hangs forever (no timeout), the loop never advances! A hanging TCP connection to workers.dev would do exactly that. So add AbortSignal.timeout(10000) to every fetch in smoke script, and timeout-minutes: 6 on the smoke step.

Let me wait for the job to finish (maybe it eventually fails) — or directly patch now: add timeout-minutes to the smoke step and AbortSignal.timeout(15000) on all fetches in the smoke script. Then push. The current hanging run will be superseded.

name: deploy-staging

# Deploys the Worker + D1 to the STAGING environment and runs real-Cloudflare
# smoke tests. Requires two GitHub Actions secrets (never committed):
#   CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN  — API token with D1:Edit + Workers Scripts:Edit
#   CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID — account identifier (not a secret, kept out of git anyway)
# Until both are configured, this job skips itself.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  deploy-staging:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      enabled: ${{ steps.guard.outputs.enabled }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"
      - id: guard
        env:
          CF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CF_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$CF_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$CF_ACCOUNT" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "::warning::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID not configured — staging deploy skipped"
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
      - name: Install worker deps
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        run: npm install --legacy-peer-deps --no-fund --no-audit > npm-install.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 25 npm-install.log; exit 1; }
      - name: Create D1 staging database (idempotent)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          npx wrangler d1 list --json > d1list.json || echo "[]" > d1list.json
          if ! grep -q '"name": "chatapp-staging"' d1list.json; then
            npx wrangler d1 create chatapp-staging
          fi
          npx wrangler d1 list --json > d1list.json
          node -e "const l=require('./d1list.json');const d=l.find(x=>x.name==='chatapp-staging');if(!d)process.exit(1);console.log(d.uuid)" > d1-id.txt
          echo "D1 database: $(cat d1-id.txt)"
      - name: Render staging config
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        run: |
          sed "s/__D1_DATABASE_ID__/$(cat d1-id.txt)/" wrangler.staging.template.jsonc > wrangler.staging.jsonc
          echo "config rendered (database id not committed to git)"
      - name: Apply migrations to real staging D1
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: npx wrangler d1 migrations apply chatapp-staging --remote --config wrangler.staging.jsonc
      - name: Verify migrations landed on real D1
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          npx wrangler d1 execute chatapp-staging --remote --config wrangler.staging.jsonc --json --command "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'" > tables.json
          node -e "
            const out = require('./tables.json');
            const tables = (out[0].results || []).map(r => r.name);
            const need = ['accounts','devices','signed_prekeys','one_time_prekeys','kyber_prekeys','message_queue','attachments','attachment_delivery','backups','auth_challenges','auth_tokens','rate_limits'];
            const missing = need.filter(t => !tables.includes(t));
            if (missing.length) { console.error('missing tables:', missing); process.exit(1); }
            console.log('all 12 tables present on real D1');
          "
      - name: Deploy Worker to staging
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        id: deploy
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: |
          npx wrangler deploy --config wrangler.staging.jsonc | tee deploy.log
          sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' deploy.log > deploy-clean.log
          url=$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.workers\.dev' deploy-clean.log | head -1)
          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
            sub=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" \
              "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/workers/subdomain" \
              | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{try{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log(j.result.subdomain||'')}catch{console.log('')}})")
            if [ -n "$sub" ]; then url="https://chatapp-staging.$sub.workers.dev"; fi
          fi
          if [ -z "$url" ]; then
            echo "::error::could not determine staging URL"
            tail -n 20 deploy-clean.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "staging url: $url"
      - name: Run real-Cloudflare smoke tests
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        timeout-minutes: 6
        env:
          STAGING_URL: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
          STAGING_TOKEN_TTL_MS: "20000"
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          node test/smoke-staging.mjs 2>&1 | tee smoke.log || true
          echo "--- smoke.log size: $(wc -c < smoke.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0) bytes, lines: $(wc -l < smoke.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
          if [ ! -s smoke.log ]; then
            echo "::error::smoke.log is empty — node produced no output"
          fi
          if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
            grep -E "STEP|PASS|FAIL|never|crashed" smoke.log | head -n 30 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.320s' "$l")"; done
            if ! grep -qE "STEP|PASS|FAIL" smoke.log; then
              tail -n 10 smoke.log | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE-RAW: $(printf '%.320s' "$l")"; done
            fi
            exit 1
          fi

The crash was at http() line 54 — during a POST. `fetch(`${BASE}${path}`)` — `${BASE}${path}` = "https://chatapp-staging.xxx.workers.dev" + "/auth/verify" ✓ non-empty...

Unless `path` was empty! Which http() call passes an empty path? None...

Hold on — `input: ''` at line 105:21 = the fetch in http(). Hmm — unless `BASE` itself became empty DUE TO the `-replace` PowerShell patch mangling `${BASE}`! PowerShell's `-replace` uses regex replacement strings where `$` is special! In the replacement string, `${BASE}` → PowerShell tries to substitute a NAMED GROUP "BASE" → not found → replaces with EMPTY STRING!!!

YES — that's it. My PowerShell `-replace 'pattern', "const res = await fetch(`${BASE}${path}`, ..."` — in the replacement, `${BASE}` and `${path}` were interpreted as regex group references and replaced with empty strings! So the smoke script now has `const res = await fetch("", { method, headers, ... })` — empty URL!

Same for `${BASE}/devices/me` in waitUntilReachable → became `fetch("/devices/me"...)`? Actually `/devices/me` is a relative URL → "Failed to parse URL from /devices/me"... but the error says input ''. The waitUntilReachable one — `-replace 'const res = await fetch\(`\$\{BASE\}/devices/me`, \{ method: "GET" \}\);', 'const res = await fetch(`${BASE}/devices/me`, ...)'` — the replacement `` `${BASE}/devices/me` `` — again `${BASE}` group ref → empty → `fetch("/devices/me")` → throws "Failed to parse URL from /devices/me"... but the first crash shows input ''. Whatever — BOTH fetch calls are broken by PowerShell backtick+${} mangling.

So the smoke script's fetches are completely broken due to my PowerShell patch. The fix: rewrite smoke-staging.mjs cleanly with the Write tool (no PowerShell string surgery). The script never crashed before this patch (34292da run reached the worker!).

- AbortSignal timeouts

The [STEPS] summary lines and [STEP] lines show the same 4 first steps — but I don't see "auth verify" STEP line. Then it stopped — meaning the script CRASHED after "auth challenge" — during buildContext("auth", ...)? No wait — the steps array only records entries added so far. The last entry is "auth challenge" — then the script crashed before stepLog("auth verify", ...).

Between stepLog("auth challenge", chA) and stepLog("auth verify", verifyA), the code does:
```ts
const ctxA = buildContext("auth", {...});
const sigA = await signB64(priv1, ctxA);
const verifyA = await http("POST", "/auth/verify", {...});
```
A crash there → caught by main().catch → "[STEPS]" dump printed → exit 1. The catch prints "smoke test crashed: ..." — which my workflow grep (\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]) would catch "[STEPS]" lines but not the crash line itself... The [STEPS] lines show only 4 steps — so crash happened right after "auth challenge" stepLog.

What could crash? signB64 — crypto.subtle.sign on the RUNNER (node) — works in miniflare test env but here it's the GitHub runner node 22 — Ed25519 in Node webcrypto: Node 22 supports Ed25519 in webcrypto? Node 18+ has Ed25519 in crypto.subtle behind... Actually Node supports Ed25519 in webcrypto since v18.4 (experimental) and stable later. Node 22 should support it.

Hmm wait — but the first "register" flow ALSO signs (signB64(priv1, ctx1)) and that worked (register account 201!). So signB64 works on the runner.

So what crashed between? `buildContext("auth", ...)` — trivial. `signB64` again — worked before. `http("POST", "/auth/verify", ...)` — fetch with AbortSignal... a fetch could throw synchronously on invalid URL, but path is fine.

Wait — the catch dumps [STEPS] and rethrows... the crash message "smoke test crashed: ..." is console.error'd — grep pattern in workflow: `grep -E "\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]"` — the crash line "smoke test crashed: ..." does NOT match [STEP]... but "[STEPS]" lines DO match \[STEP. The [STEPS] lines shown = 4 entries. So the crash error message itself wasn't shown (not matching grep). Damn.

The [SUMMARY] line: I emit `console.error('[SUMMARY] ...')` only when failures > 0 in the normal path — not in the catch path. The crash path emits [STEPS] only.

So the crash error is unknown. But note: the smoke script has try/catch? http() has no try — fetch errors propagate. With AbortSignal.timeout(15000) a TimeoutError would be thrown → caught by main().catch → crash dump. The auth verify request may be TIMING OUT on real Cloudflare — 15s timeout!

Why would /auth/verify hang on real Cloudflare? It does D1 queries + Ed25519 verify... D1 queries on staging DB... 

Hmm wait — actually, why would it hang? Rate limit? No — 429 returns fast.

OK here's the thing — I've been going back and forth through annotations, each cycle costing minutes. The user is frustrated ("1 ساعته گفت ادامه بده"). The most effective approach: change the workflow to dump the ENTIRE smoke.log as an artifact AND print the crash line by fixing the grep pattern to include "crashed". Actually simpler: the catch prints "smoke test crashed: <message>" — add "crashed" to the workflow grep. It was there before but I changed it.

Let me update grep to: `grep -E "\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|Error"` and also always print the last 5 lines raw. Actually the current workflow already prints SMOKE-RAW tail -10 when no [STEP]... but [STEP] existed so raw wasn't printed.

Change: always print the crash line: `grep -E "crashed|Error|error" smoke.log | head -3`.

Actually — simplest hypothesis for the crash: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) fires on /auth/verify because real Cloudflare's /auth/verify HANGS. Why would it hang on real D1? 

OH WAIT. I know. `verifyEd25519(device.auth_pub_key...)` → `asBytes(device.auth_pub_key)` — if real D1 returns auth_pub_key as a **string** (D1 returns BLOB as... hmm). If asBytes throws "unsupported binary shape returned by D1" → that's a THROW → HttpError? No — generic Error → errorResponse → 500 INTERNAL JSON response. That's a RESPONSE, not a crash. And the [STEP] line would show status=500. But there's NO auth verify STEP line at all — the request never completed or crashed before.

Hmm, `http()` — `await fetch(BASE + path, {...})` — could throw if... AbortSignal timeout — 15s → step shows 2m33s?? The whole step was ~2-3 min. If verify hung 15s then threw → caught in main().catch → [STEPS] dumped → the [STEPS] would include "auth challenge" as last — MATCHES! And the crash message would say "The operation was aborted due to timeout" — printed via console.error "smoke test crashed: ..." — not in annotations due to grep.

So: /auth/verify HANGS >15s on real Cloudflare. Why? 

OH! I think I finally see it. `requireActiveDevice` → D1 query. `consumeChallenge` → D1. Then `verifyEd25519` → crypto. Then `issueToken` → D1. None obviously hang...

BUT — wait: **D1 write conflicts / row-level locking with the rate-limit upsert?** The verify handler doesn't rate-limit... hmm.

Actually — real possibility: **the staging worker deployment from run N is being replaced by run N+1's deploy while smoke runs?** No, sequential.

Alternatively — the FIRST attempt hung on `waitUntilReachable`... no, register worked.

The latest run (c255c51) TIMED OUT after 6 minutes. So the smoke script hung. The previous run (17fdf62-era, before my chA fix) crashed instantly at chA.res.body.

Now with the chA fix, the flow proceeds past auth challenge → verify... and hangs somewhere. Where?

The verify on real Cloudflare — remember the earlier 500 INTERNAL from run 34292da (pre-asBytes). Now with asBytes deployed, verify... if it 500s, `http()` returns 500 (no hang). If verify HANGS server-side (D1 deadlock?)... 

Wait — what if the hang is the EXPIRY WAIT? `token1Expires = reg.body.token_expires_at` — token_expires_at = issue + 20s (staging TTL). At the point of the expiry wait, elapsed since issue ≈ 3-5s → wait ≈ 16-18s + 1.5s ≈ 19s. Not 6 min.

What if `reg.body.token_expires_at` is a HUGE number? now = Date.now() on server. Fine.

Hmm — what about `waitUntilReachable` at the very start: if the worker was just redeployed, first requests may... 10 attempts × 3s = 30s max. Fine.

So where does 6 minutes go? The step timeout fired. The script hung somewhere WITHOUT hitting the 15s AbortSignal — meaning it hung in code that does NOT fetch: `crypto.subtle.generateKey`? `signB64`? `sleep`?

`sleep(wait)` where wait = NaN → setTimeout(NaN) → immediate. wait = Infinity? `Math.max(0, token1Expires - Date.now()) + 1500` — if token1Expires is undefined → NaN → NaN. If it's a huge number → wait huge → HANG! When would token_expires_at be huge? `issueToken(db, deviceId, now, tokenTtl)` with tokenTtl = Number(env.TOKEN_TTL_MS) = 20000 → now + 20000. Fine...

UNLESS env.TOKEN_TTL_MS is set on PRODUCTION-style... no, staging var = 20000 ✓.

Hmm — `await sleep(wait)` — if `wait` is, say, 2000000000 (huge) — hang for 23 days! token_expires_at = now + ttlMs where now = Date.now() ≈ 1.789e12 and ttl 20000 → 1.789e12. Fine.

But WAIT — what if `reg.body.token_expires_at` is fine but... the smoke script computes `wait = token1Expires - Date.now() + 1500`. token1Expires ≈ Date.now() + 20000 → wait ≈ 21500 ✓.

I'm stuck on hang location from annotations alone. The 6-min timeout with the previous run crashing instantly at chA.res.body suggests the chA fix works and flow proceeds... into auth verify which may now work or hang...

The most productive next step: reduce annotation noise and get the ACTUAL verify response. Let me modify the smoke script to log EVERY http() response status immediately (stepLog called inside http for every call — cheap and complete), cap annotations correctly, and extend timeout-minutes to 10.

Actually — better idea: the smoke step timeout of 6 min might be hit because of the expiry wait PLUS preceding steps... no.

Hmm — one more idea: `waitUntilReachable` GETs /devices/me WITHOUT auth → my router: authenticate throws UNAUTHORIZED → 401 ✓ returns. Loop exits on first 401 ✓.

OK here's my decision: instrument http() to log every request status INSIDE the script (so even hangs before stepLog show the last completed request), push, and run once more. If it hangs again, the last logged request identifies the hanging endpoint. That's the definitive diagnostic.

The smoke test timed out again at 6 minutes. But now the [HTTP] log lines are in smoke.log — however the annotations were emitted via the grep AFTER the step timed out... when a step times out, does the `run:` block's subsequent annotation emission still happen? No — when the step times out, the process is killed, so the annotations after the node command never execute. That's why no [HTTP] annotations appear!

The step structure is wrong for debugging: node hangs → timeout kills → no annotations emitted.

I need to restructure: run the smoke script with its own internal timeout so it EXITS (producing annotations... no wait, annotations are emitted by the workflow steps, and ::error:: from node's console.error WOULD be processed if node prints them before being killed).

The node script prints [HTTP] lines as it goes. If it hangs at request N, lines 1..N-1 are already printed to stdout → tee writes them to smoke.log. When the step is killed at 6 min, the emitted ::error:: annotations from node's console.error... node prints [HTTP] via console.log (not ::error::) — annotations only come from ::error:: syntax. The node script doesn't emit ::error::. So no annotations — consistent with what we see.

Solution: make the node script emit `::error::` for EVERY http line directly (so annotations stream in real-time as each request completes), AND make the script have a hard internal deadline (e.g., 4 minutes via a global timer that exits(1) printing all collected lines) so it always exits BEFORE the 6-min step timeout.

Let me restructure smoke-staging.mjs:
- collect all [HTTP] lines into an array
- global watchdog: setTimeout(4*60*1000) → print all collected lines with ::error:: prefix + exit(1). Use unref? No — must fire. But setTimeout keeps process alive — fine, it's our watchdog. But if the script finishes normally before, clear it or let it be cleared via process.exit in main.
- http() logs via console.log AND pushes to the array, AND emits ::error:: with the [HTTP] line immediately? Emitting ::error:: for successful requests pollutes but guarantees visibility. Cap: annotations max ~13 shown... 11 requests total — OK under 13!

Actually the cap: GH shows max 13 annotations per check run? We've seen exactly 13 multiple times. 11 requests + node warning = 12 ✓ fits.

Let me emit each [HTTP] line as ::error:: — wait, that makes the build show 11 "errors" even on success... they'd show as annotations on the check run. On success, still shown but the run is green. Acceptable for debugging; I'll switch to ::warning:: to be less alarming, but warnings also count toward cap and DO show. Hmm — do warnings show? Yes, the node-deprecation warning shows. OK — use ::warning:: for [HTTP] lines. But wait — earlier PASS lines came through as ::error:: (I emitted them via grep ::error::). Warnings should work too.

Also add the global watchdog with ::error:: dump of all lines.

Push, run once — the [HTTP] lines will show exactly which request hangs.

parts.text: Now add the `wrangler tail` capture to the smoke step and a watchdog in the smoke script:

input.newString:
- name: Run real-Cloudflare smoke tests (with wrangler tail capture)
        if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        working-directory: backend/worker
        timeout-minutes: 7
        env:
          STAGING_URL: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
          STAGING_TOKEN_TTL_MS: "20000"
        run: |
          npx wrangler tail chatapp-staging --format pretty > tail.log 2>&1 &
          TAIL_PID=$!
          sleep 5
          node test/smoke-staging.mjs 2>&1 | tee smoke.log || true
          kill $TAIL_PID 2>/dev/null || true
          sleep 2
          echo "captured tail: $(wc -l < tail.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0) lines"
          if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
            grep -E "\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|TimeoutError|AbortError|Error:" smoke.log | head -n 12 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Dump wrangler tail on failure
        if: failure()
        working-directory: backend/worker
        run: |
          if [ -s tail.log ]; then
            grep -iE "error|exception|throw|Unhandled" tail.log | head -n 10 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::TAIL: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
          fi

parts.text:
Now I have the FULL real-Cloudflare trace:

```
POST /auth/challenge → 200 ✅
POST /accounts → 201 ✅ (Ed25519 verified on real Workers)
GET /devices/me → 200 ✅ (D1 persistence)
POST /auth/challenge → 409 USERNAME_TAKEN ✅ (dup)
POST /auth/verify → 500 INTERNAL ❌ (persists even after asBytes widening!)
POST /auth/challenge (add_device) → 200 ✅
POST /devices → 401 INVALID_SIGNATURE ❌ (still!)
GET /devices/me → 401 UNAUTHORIZED (correct — no token)
POST /auth/challenge → 200 (accountB register challenge)
...HANG (timeout at 7 min)
```

Also `wrangler tail` failed instantly: "In a non-interactive environment, it's necessary to set a CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" — the tail command ran in a subshell without the env (I didn't pass CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN to that step's tail background command — actually the step HAS env CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN? No! The smoke step env only has STAGING_URL and STAGING_TOKEN_TTL_MS. The tail process needs CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN too. Need to add.

And the HANG: the smoke script hung AFTER the last challenge — at POST /accounts for accountB. The previous run also hung at the same place. So **POST /accounts hangs on the SECOND call from the same run** (first one worked!). What's different? The rate limit upsert: first register → INSERT (new row, no conflict). Second register (10+ min later? No — same run, same window!) → ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE path with RETURNING. In miniflare, the upsert conflict path... in the worker-tests the rate-limit test DID test the conflict path (bucket test-bucket) and it worked in miniflare ✓. On REAL D1, `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` might behave differently... or DEADLOCK/hang?

Actually — wait. On real D1, could the issue be that `first()` on a statement with RETURNING... hmm.

Actually, more likely: on real D1 the auth verify 500 and the /accounts hang could share a root cause: **the D1 "sessions" API vs first()?** No...

Let me think about verify 500 more carefully with the new asBytes. What shapes can real D1 return for BLOB auth_pub_key?
- If it returns a base64 STRING → asBytes decodes ✓ → verify proceeds... then what else could throw? `crypto.subtle.importKey` with the decoded bytes ✓...

Hmm wait — what if the BLOB comes back as a **number array-like object** my new code handles ✓. What if it comes back as `{"0":..,"1":..}` without length... my Array.isArray(o.data) fails → throw → 500 ✓ still matches.

I need the REAL error. wrangler tail is the tool — fix the env for tail:
- Pass CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN/CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID into the smoke step env (it already has STAGING_URL etc. — add the two secrets).
- Also tail needs `--format json` and works non-interactively with the token ✓.

Also — the hang at second /accounts: could ALSO be visible in tail (request received but no response).

And per user rule: "اگر ناسازگاری وجود داشت، قبل از Phase بعدی implementation را متوقف کن" — the real-D1 BLOB shape difference IS a Miniflare↔Cloudflare incompatibility to report. But I can still debug within Phase 1.5 — that's the point of staging. Let me fix tail env + push + rerun to capture the real verify exception.

Actually — I can ALSO test the deployed worker MYSELF right now via webfetch! GET https://chatapp-staging.<sub>.workers.dev/devices/me → 401 UNAUTHORIZED proves it's live. But I don't know the subdomain... The annotations didn't print it (deploy step printed "staging url:" to step log). Hmm.

Wait — actually I CAN check something: the smoke script's failed verify happened against the live worker — the URL exists. Let me just fix tail env, add TOKEN passthrough, and rerun. The tail will show the exception.

One more improvement for the hang: the smoke script watchdog — add a 4-minute hard timeout inside the script that dumps steps and exits 1. This prevents the 7-min step timeout and gives us [STEPS] + crash context. But actually the hang was AFTER [HTTP] #9 — a watchdog at 4 min would fire and dump — good enough combined with tail.

Actually the REAL fix for the hang might be simpler: POST /accounts hang = D1 upsert... Let me look at checkRateLimit's SQL: `ON CONFLICT (bucket, key) DO UPDATE SET count = CASE WHEN window_start = ?3 THEN count + 1 ELSE 1 END, window_start = ?3 RETURNING count` — binding ?3 used three times ✓ fine. Real D1 supports upsert+RETURNING? Should. But — hmm, "INSERT OR ... ON CONFLICT (bucket, key)" — the PK is (bucket,key) ✓.

Could the hang be Cloudflare's D1 write-coalescing... I'll get the tail. Fix and push.
دو مشکل باقی‌مانده مشخص شد: (1) `wrangler tail` بدون `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` در env اجرا شد، (2) verify همچنان 500 می‌دهد. tail را با env صحیح اصلاح می‌کنم تا exception واقعی سرور را ببینیم:

          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}

        run: |

            exit 1
          fi

parts.text:
Now I have the full trace with the tail capture. The sequence:

1. POST /auth/challenge → 200 ✅
2. POST /accounts → 201 ✅
3. GET /devices/me → 200 ✅
4. POST /auth/challenge → 409 USERNAME_TAKEN ✅ (duplicate — the smoke script reuses the same username in the dup check ✓ correct)
5. POST /auth/verify → **500 INTERNAL** ❌ (STILL fails with asBytes widened!)
6. POST /auth/challenge (add_device) → 200 ✅
7. POST /devices → **401 INVALID_SIGNATURE** ❌
8. GET /devices/me → 401 UNAUTHORIZED ✅ (correct — token undefined after failed add)
9. POST /auth/challenge → 200 (accountB register challenge — wait, this shouldn't succeed... username = smoke_b_<runStart> unique ✓)
10. ... then HUNG (timeout at 7 min) — at POST /accounts for accountB presumably (rate limit accounts_ip: 3 per 10 min — the runner IP: registers: #1 (account1) + #2 (accountB) — wait, only 2... but challenge_ip: challenges issued from the runner IP: register(1) + dup(2) + add(3) + authB(4) = 4 < 10 ✓. Hmm — but wait: previous RUNS within the last 10 min also counted! Runs are ~15 min apart mostly, windows reset... 

The HANG at POST /accounts for accountB: rate-limit checks pass, consume passes, verify passes(?), then createAccountWithDevice batch → D1... Hmm. OR the hang is in `sha256HexOf`/`issueToken`... 

BUT the tail.log dump step didn't show TAIL annotations! The "Dump wrangler tail on failure" step ran (if: failure()) — its grep found nothing matching, or tail.log was empty (tail needs a few seconds to attach; the wrangler tail process was started with & then killed after smoke — the kill + only 3s wait... tail.log might have content). The annotations show NO TAIL lines — the dump step emitted "::error::tail.log empty or missing"? NOT present. Hmm — actually the annotations list only shows 13 max... the visible ones are all SMOKE [HTTP]/[STEP] + the timeout. The TAIL ::error:: might be beyond the cap (13). Ugh.

OK — different approach to get the real verify exception: **the worker itself catches errors and returns 500 INTERNAL without detail (by design — no leakage). For debugging, staging needs a debug mode**: add env var DEBUG_ERRORS="true" on staging that includes the error message + stack in the 500 response. That's staging-only (vars, not secrets) and gives us the exact exception in the smoke log. This is a standard staging pattern.

Let me add:
- router errorResponse: if env.DEBUG_ERRORS → include message and stack.
- staging config template: vars DEBUG_ERRORS: "true".

Then the smoke [STEP]/[HTTP] annotation for verify will show the real error message. 

Also for the HANG: with DEBUG_ERRORS we'll see. The hang on POST /accounts (accountB)... interesting: accountB's register → rate limit accounts_ip: the FIRST register from this IP → count=1 ✓. consume ✓ → verifyEd25519 with accountB's key ✓ → username check ✓ → batch insert... could hang if D1 write contention on... Hmm, actually — wait. Look at the sequence again: the hang happened right after accountB's challenge (200). So POST /accounts for accountB hung. But the FIRST POST /accounts worked fine. What's different? accountB's registration_id=1000 (same), username different... 

OH WAIT!!! I see it — `createAccountWithDevice` → `db.batch([...])` — fine. But the HANG could be... the `crypto.getRandomValues`... no.

Hmm — actually, could the hang be in `checkRateLimit`'s upsert with `RETURNING count`? First register: INSERT (no conflict) path. accountB: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE path — this is the FIRST time the conflict path runs on real D1! Maybe real D1 hangs/errors on `RETURNING` with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE? If it errored → 500. If it HANGS → the request hangs ✓ MATCHES!

And the verify 500: different cause — the BLOB shape. Two separate real-D1 issues.

But wait — in miniflare both work. The rate-limit upsert conflict path worked in worker-tests (miniflare) ✓. On real D1 it hangs → that's the Miniflare↔D1 incompatibility.

Hmm — actually, is it possible real D1 doesn't support `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`? D1 is SQLite-based; RETURNING is supported since SQLite 3.35 ✓ D1 uses newer. But the combination... The verify 500 is definitely an exception.

Debug plan (staging debug mode):
1. tokens.ts/router: pass debug flag through.
2. router errorResponse: if env.DEBUG_ERRORS === "true", include `debug: { message: e.message, stack: e.stack }` in the 500 body.
3. staging template vars: DEBUG_ERRORS: "true".
4. smoke script: print full body on 500s (it already logs [HTTP] without body — the [STEP] log shows JSON.stringify(res.body).slice(0,160) — for a 500 with debug stack it'd be truncated... increase slice for 500s or print error.debug.stack separately).

Also for the HANG: the accounts_ip rate limit — wait, actually let me reconsider the hang. accountB's POST /accounts — hmm, wait: does the smoke script actually issue accountB's register? YES via the inline flow. The HANG... 

Actually — maybe the hang is the D1 upsert DEADLOCK with itself: checkRateLimit(accounts_global) and checkRateLimit(accounts_ip) — two upserts on DIFFERENT rows — fine.

OR the verify 500 error was thrown DURING a D1 batch leaving... no.

Let me just add DEBUG_ERRORS and see. Also add a 500 debug for the hang? Hangs don't return...

For the hang — wrangler tail with proper env might capture it. But tail.log dump step: cap 13 might hide TAIL lines... The failure dump step is a SEPARATE step — its annotations compete within the same check run (13 cap total). The SMOKE grep emits up to 12... TAIL gets crowded out. Fix: in the smoke step, reduce emitted diagnostics to ~6; then TAIL dump gets 6-7 slots.

Actually — better: put the tail dump INTO the smoke step itself (same step, after kill): the tail.log grep emissions happen within the same step — still same check run cap. Hmm.

The cap is 13 per check run (per annotation list). Current failure run emitted: 12 SMOKE + timeout + node-deprecated = 14 → capped at 13. If I limit SMOKE to 6 and TAIL dump to 6 → fits.

Let me restructure:
- smoke step failure diagnostics: only the [STEP] verify line + [HTTP] verify line (6 max)
- tail dump: 6 lines

Also — DEBUG_ERRORS addition is the key unlock. Implement:

router.ts:
```ts
} catch (e) {
  if (env.DEBUG_ERRORS === "true" && e instanceof Error) {
    return jsonResponse({ error: { code: "INTERNAL", message: e.message, stack: e.stack } }, 500);
  }
  return errorResponse(e);
}
```

staging template vars: DEBUG_ERRORS: "true".

smoke script: on 500, print the full body (including stack) via ::error:: — the [STEP] line slice(0,160) too small — for status >= 500 print full JSON. Let me make stepLog print body fully when status >= 500.

Also handleVerify 500 → smoke script continues (check fails, no throw) → add_device proceeds → hang at accountB register. With DEBUG_ERRORS the verify 500 body will name the exception.

Let me also think about what the verify exception could be, so maybe I fix it directly: 

In handleVerify: `requireActiveDevice` returns row with auth_pub_key as BLOB → real D1 shape issue → asBytes handles most... What if real D1 returns BLOB as `null`?? If the INSERT bound a Uint8Array and real D1 stored it, read returns ArrayBuffer. Hmm.

What if `.first<{...}>()` on real D1 with a BLOB column returns the row but auth_pub_key is... an object like {type:"Buffer",data:[...]}? asBytes handles ✓.

What if it returns a base64 STRING? asBytes handles ✓ (decodes).

Hmm — so what throws? Maybe nothing in verify logic — maybe the 500 is from... `consumeChallenge` → the UPDATE with subquery on real D1... worked in register ✓.

`issueToken` INSERT auth_tokens — fine.

Hmm wait — actually, maybe the verify 500 happens BEFORE all that: the rate limit? Verify has no rate limit ✓. JSON parse ✓. 

OR — `ctx.now`! NOW_OVERRIDE_MS not set ✓ → Date.now() ✓.

OK — DEBUG_ERRORS will tell us. Implement now:
1. router.ts: DEBUG_ERRORS handling (need env in catch — restructure handleRequest to catch within itself where env is in scope ✓ it is).
2. staging template: DEBUG_ERRORS var.
3. smoke stepLog: full body for status >= 500.
4. Reduce SMOKE annotation spam: grep only lines with "status=5" or "INVALID" or "STEP"... simpler: keep as-is but limit to 8; TAIL dump 5.

Push, rerun, read the real error.

Index: .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml
===================================================================
--- .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml	
+++ .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml	
@@ -1,139 +1,140 @@
 name: deploy-staging
 
 # Deploys the Worker + D1 to the STAGING environment and runs real-Cloudflare
 # smoke tests. Requires two GitHub Actions secrets (never committed):
 #   CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN  â€” API token with D1:Edit + Workers Scripts:Edit
 #   CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID â€” account identifier (not a secret, kept out of git anyway)
 # Until both are configured, this job skips itself.
 
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main]
   workflow_dispatch:
 
 jobs:
   deploy-staging:
     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
     outputs:
       enabled: ${{ steps.guard.outputs.enabled }}
     steps:
       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
       - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
         with:
           node-version: "22"
       - id: guard
         env:
           CF_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CF_ACCOUNT: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           if [ -n "$CF_TOKEN" ] && [ -n "$CF_ACCOUNT" ]; then
             echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           else
             echo "::warning::CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN / CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID not configured â€” staging deploy skipped"
             echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           fi
       - name: Install worker deps
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         run: npm install --legacy-peer-deps --no-fund --no-audit > npm-install.log 2>&1 || { tail -n 25 npm-install.log; exit 1; }
       - name: Create D1 staging database (idempotent)
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler d1 list --json > d1list.json || echo "[]" > d1list.json
           if ! grep -q '"name": "chatapp-staging"' d1list.json; then
             npx wrangler d1 create chatapp-staging
           fi
           npx wrangler d1 list --json > d1list.json
           node -e "const l=require('./d1list.json');const d=l.find(x=>x.name==='chatapp-staging');if(!d)process.exit(1);console.log(d.uuid)" > d1-id.txt
           echo "D1 database: $(cat d1-id.txt)"
       - name: Render staging config
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         run: |
           sed "s/__D1_DATABASE_ID__/$(cat d1-id.txt)/" wrangler.staging.template.jsonc > wrangler.staging.jsonc
           echo "config rendered (database id not committed to git)"
       - name: Apply migrations to real staging D1
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: npx wrangler d1 migrations apply chatapp-staging --remote --config wrangler.staging.jsonc
       - name: Verify migrations landed on real D1
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler d1 execute chatapp-staging --remote --config wrangler.staging.jsonc --json --command "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'" > tables.json
           node -e "
             const out = require('./tables.json');
             const tables = (out[0].results || []).map(r => r.name);
             const need = ['accounts','devices','signed_prekeys','one_time_prekeys','kyber_prekeys','message_queue','attachments','attachment_delivery','backups','auth_challenges','auth_tokens','rate_limits'];
             const missing = need.filter(t => !tables.includes(t));
             if (missing.length) { console.error('missing tables:', missing); process.exit(1); }
             console.log('all 12 tables present on real D1');
           "
       - name: Deploy Worker to staging
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         id: deploy
         env:
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler deploy --config wrangler.staging.jsonc | tee deploy.log
           sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' deploy.log > deploy-clean.log
           url=$(grep -oE 'https://[a-z0-9-]+\.workers\.dev' deploy-clean.log | head -1)
           if [ -z "$url" ]; then
             sub=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN" \
               "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID/workers/subdomain" \
               | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c);process.stdin.on('end',()=>{try{const j=JSON.parse(d);console.log(j.result.subdomain||'')}catch{console.log('')}})")
             if [ -n "$sub" ]; then url="https://chatapp-staging.$sub.workers.dev"; fi
           fi
           if [ -z "$url" ]; then
             echo "::error::could not determine staging URL"
             tail -n 20 deploy-clean.log
             exit 1
           fi
           echo "url=$url" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "staging url: $url"
       - name: Run real-Cloudflare smoke tests (with wrangler tail capture)
         if: steps.guard.outputs.enabled == 'true'
         working-directory: backend/worker
         timeout-minutes: 7
         env:
           STAGING_URL: ${{ steps.deploy.outputs.url }}
           STAGING_TOKEN_TTL_MS: "20000"
           CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
           CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
         run: |
           npx wrangler tail chatapp-staging --format pretty > tail.log 2>&1 &
           TAIL_PID=$!
           sleep 8
           node test/smoke-staging.mjs 2>&1 | tee smoke.log || true
           kill $TAIL_PID 2>/dev/null || true
           sleep 3
           echo "captured tail: $(wc -l < tail.log 2>/dev/null || echo 0) lines"
           if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
-            grep -E "\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|TimeoutError|AbortError|Error:" smoke.log | head -n 12 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
+            grep "\[DEBUG500\]" smoke.log | head -n 4 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::DEBUG500: $(printf '%.1000s' "$l")"; done
+            grep -cE "\[STEP\]" smoke.log | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::steps completed: $l"; done
             exit 1
           fi
       - name: Dump wrangler tail on failure
         if: failure()
         working-directory: backend/worker
         run: |
           if [ -s tail.log ]; then
             grep -iE "Exception|error|throw|Unhandled|\"outcome\"" tail.log | grep -vE "GET /devices/me -> 401" | head -n 15 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::TAIL: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
           else
             echo "::error::tail.log empty or missing"
           fi
           if ! grep -q "ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED" smoke.log; then
             grep -E "\[HTTP\]|\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|TimeoutError|AbortError" smoke.log | head -n 12 | while IFS= read -r l; do echo "::error::SMOKE: $(printf '%.300s' "$l")"; done
             exit 1
           fi

parts.text:
Now I have the FULL chronological HTTP trace from two runs (this one and the previous one at lines 20-56):

Run timeline (this run, chronological):
1. POST /auth/challenge → 200 ✓
2. POST /accounts → 201 ✓
3. GET /devices/me → 200 ✓
4. POST /auth/challenge → **500 INTERNAL** ❌ (this is the "duplicate username" check! The 409 USERNAME_TAKEN path threw!)
5. POST /auth/verify → 500 ❌
6. POST /auth/challenge (add_device) → 200 ✓
7. POST /devices → 500 ❌
8. GET /devices/me (no auth) → 500 ❌
...then hang → 7 min timeout.

Previous run (lines 20-56, chronological):
1. POST /auth/challenge → 200 ✓
2. POST /accounts → 201 ✓
3. GET /devices/me → 200 ✓
4. POST /auth/challenge → 200 (hmm, this was the dup — 200? In the previous run the username was unique so no 409)
5. POST /auth/verify → 500 ❌
6. POST /auth/challenge → 200
7. POST /devices → 500 ❌
8. GET /devices/me → 500 ❌
9. POST /auth/challenge → 200
then hang.

PATTERN FOUND: **POST /accounts works ONCE. Everything after that which touches D1 with... fails with 500, EXCEPT /auth/challenge (which only does SELECT + INSERT into auth_challenges).**

What do the failing endpoints have in common vs the working ones?
- ✅ /auth/challenge: SELECT accounts, INSERT auth_challenges — works repeatedly
- ✅ POST /accounts (first): rate-limit upserts, consume UPDATE, SELECT, batch INSERT×3 — works ONCE
- ❌ POST /auth/verify: consume UPDATE (already consumed → 401? no — this is a FRESH auth challenge... wait in this run the auth verify followed the 500 at dup-challenge. The verify's consume UPDATE + SELECT device + issueToken INSERT → 500
- ❌ POST /devices: INSERT..SELECT + token INSERT → 500
- ❌ GET /devices/me: SELECT by token_hash → 500!!! 

**GET /devices/me with a VALID token → 500.** It reads `auth_tokens` by token_hash! And the first /accounts worked but inserted into auth_tokens...

Pattern: everything that QUERIES `auth_tokens` → 500. /auth/challenge doesn't touch auth_tokens ✓ works. POST /accounts inserts into auth_tokens (batch) — first worked, but subsequent reads fail.

What could make SELECT from auth_tokens throw on real D1 but not miniflare? 

**IDEA: the `token_hash` TEXT PK with a SHA-256 hex string — fine. But WAIT — maybe the issue is the auth_tokens FK: `device_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices(device_id)` — reading is fine...

Hmm, what about D1's "no such table" if the MIGRATIONS ran on a different D1?? No — migrations verified 12 tables on chatapp-staging ✓ and the deploy used the same config ✓.

**BETTER IDEA: the DEBUG_ERRORS 500 body contains the actual message+stack — and the smoke script PRINTS it via [STEP]!** Look at the [STEP] lines: "devices/me with token1 status=200" — the 200 one. But the FAILING requests were logged via [HTTP] which does NOT print the body! Only [STEP] prints the body (slice 160). The failing requests (verify 500, devices/me 500) have NO [STEP] because the script's flow checks failed... 

Wait — verify: `const verify = await http(...); stepLog("auth verify", verify)` — hmm, in the SMOKE script the verify flow: after `chA` the script does ctx/sign/verify/stepLog. But in THIS run the dup-challenge returned 500 (not 409!) → `expect(dup.status === 409...)` — WAIT, smoke uses check() not expect... the dup check: `check("duplicate username rejected (409)", dup.status === 409...)` — records failure, continues ✓. Then the AUTH section: chA (auth challenge for device_id — but the account WAS created ✓ 200), verify → 500 → stepLog("auth verify", verify) — [STEP] with body... the [STEP] annotation for verify: NOT in the annotations list — the annotations show [HTTP] verify 500 but no [STEP] verify — because the cap (13) cut them? The annotations list: 13 entries total. The [STEP] verify would be #14. DAMN the cap.

But the workflow's diagnostic grep emits: WWW window (6) + ... hmm the grep pattern in deploy-staging is `\[STEP\]|\[SUMMARY\]|crashed|...` — the [STEP] verify line with the DEBUG body (which contains the real error message!) should be within the first 12... The annotations I fetched show [HTTP] lines but NOT the [STEP] verify line. The grep emits in FILE ORDER: grep outputs lines in file order: [STEP] register challenge(1), [STEP] register account(2), [HTTP] challenge(3), [HTTP] accounts(4), [HTTP] me(5), [HTTP] dup(6), [HTTP] verify(7), [STEP] verify(8!!) — should be included in head -12...

Unless [STEP] verify wasn't emitted because the script CRASHED before stepLog? In THIS run the flow: dup challenge 500 → check fails (no throw) → auth section: chA 200 → ctx/sign → verify 500 → stepLog ✓... then `check("auth verify issued a second token", verify.status === 200 && verify.body.device_id === device1...)` — `verify.body.device_id` — verify.body = {error:{...}} → device_id undefined → check false ✓ no throw. Then add_device section: chD 200 → ctxD → sigs → add 500 → stepLog ✓ → me2: `http("GET", "/devices/me", { token: add.body.token })` — add.body.token undefined → token undefined → `if (opts.token)` false → no auth header ✓ → me2 500 → ... then accountB register: chB 200, then `registerAccount`? No — inline: regB = http accounts → 500? The [HTTP] lines in the tail window show "POST /devices → 500" and "GET /devices/me → 500" and "POST /auth/challenge → 200"... then hang.

OK — I NEED the [STEP] verify body with the stack. The annotation cap is killing me. Let me change the workflow diagnostics to ONLY emit [DEBUG500]/[STEP]-with-500 lines (max 3-4), guaranteeing they fit under the cap.

Actually — better: emit the WWW window from smoke.log filtered to lines containing "stack" — the DEBUG500 body contains "stack". New grep: `grep -E '\[DEBUG500\]' smoke.log | head -4`.

Also the HANG: after accountB challenge (200), POST /accounts for accountB — with DEBUG_ERRORS, if it 500s it returns... it HUNG. What in /accounts could hang on real D1? The rate-limit upsert on `rate_limits` — the ONLY rate-limit call... /auth/challenge also does checkRateLimit (challenge_ip) — worked (200 repeatedly!). So the upsert works. 

Hmm wait — /auth/challenge DOES call checkRateLimit (challenge_ip bucket) → upsert → works every time ✓. POST /accounts: accounts_ip upsert (same bucket style, different bucket) ✓ + accounts_global ✓... those work on the FIRST /accounts. On the SECOND /accounts (accountB), the upserts hit the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE path — the FIRST /accounts did INSERT (fresh). So: **ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE + RETURNING on real D1 = hang?!** That matches: verify 500 (exception) + /accounts hang on the conflict path!

Hmm wait — but the worker-tests job (miniflare) tested the conflict path ✓ works. Real D1 divergence.

Hmm, but actually — /auth/verify ALSO hits a conflict: consumeChallenge on an... no — the auth challenge was fresh (never consumed) → UPDATE affects 1 row → not a conflict path. But it 500'd anyway!

So what does verify do that challenge doesn't: read devices (BLOB auth_pub_key), issueToken (INSERT auth_tokens)... 

GET /devices/me (with valid token): SELECT auth_tokens + SELECT devices → 500. It ONLY reads. A pure SELECT throwing on real D1? Unless... the token_hash = SHA-256 hex ✓...

WAIT WAIT. What if it's not the SQL — what if it's **`ctx.now`**! `Number(env.NOW_OVERRIDE_MS) > 0 ? Number(...) : Date.now()` — NOW_OVERRIDE_MS is "" → Number("") = 0 → Date.now() ✓.

Hmm what about `authenticate` — `b64ToBytes(match[1])` — match[1] = token from header — btoa-produced base64 with possible "+" and "/" — atob handles ✓.

OK I need the actual error message. The DEBUG_ERRORS body IS in smoke.log as [STEP] verify line. Let me make the workflow emit ONLY [STEP] lines containing "status=500" — guaranteed ≤ 3 annotations.

Actually — simpler: `grep "\[DEBUG500\]"` — the smoke script emits [DEBUG500] with FULL body (up to whole JSON) for any >= 500. That's the most valuable. Let me change the workflow to: `grep "\[DEBUG500\]" smoke.log | head -3` + keep 1 line for step count. 

Push and run. This will finally reveal the real exception.

الگو کاملاً مشخص شد: بعد از اولین POST /accounts موفق، هر endpointی که `auth_tokens` را می‌خواند 500 می‌دهد و POST /accounts دوم (مسیر conflict در rate-limit upsert) HANG می‌کند — این دقیقاً واگرایی Miniflare↔D1 واقعی است. باید body خطای DEBUG_ERRORS را ببینم:
